row.cell: Clean animals entered the ark by seven and seven, unclean by two and two.

cell.p: Sexe hundred ger noe was hold

Quan he dede him in ðe arche-wold;
Two ðhuſant ger, ſex hundred mo,
And ſex and fifti forð to ðo,
weren of werldes elde numen
ðan noe waſ in to ðe arche cumen.

row.cell:
[Fol. 12.]
Six hundred years old was Noah when he entered the ark.

cell.p:
Ilc watereſ ſpringe here ſtrengðe undede,
And Reyn gette dun on euerilk ſtede
fowerti daiſ and fowerti nigt,

So wex water wið magti migt;
So wunderlike it wex & get

row.cell: The water springs undid their strength. Rain poured down on every place.

cell.p:
ðat fiftene elne it ouer-flet,
Ouer ilk dune, and ouer ilc hil,

row.cell: Fifteen ells it overflowed, over every hill and vale.

cell.p: ðo waſ ilc fleiſ on wer[l]de ſlagen,
ðo gunnen ðe wateres hem wið-dragen.

row.cell: Then was all flesh destroyed.

div.p: At the end of the line in the margin 'Se archa Nœe.'

cell.p:
Ðe ſeuend moned[112] waſ in cumen,
And ſeuene and .xx.ti dais numen,
IN armenie ðat arche ſtod,
ðo waſ wið-dragen ðat ilc flod.

row.cell: In the seventh month and the twenty-seventh day the ark stood in Armenia.

cell.p: It adde leſted longe a-nog

row.cell: When the tenth month came the waters withdrew.

cell.p:
Fowerti daiſ after ðiſ,
Arches windoge undon it iſ,
ðe Rauen ut-fleg, hu ſo it gan ben,
Ne cam he nogt to ðe arche a-gen;

row.cell:
[Fol. 12b.]
Forty days after this the ark's window is undone, the raven out flew, and came not again to the ark.

ðe duue fond no clene ſtede,
And wente a-gen and wel it dede;
The dove found no clean place, and came again to the ark.

cell.p: ðe ſeuendai eſt ut it tog,

And brogt a grene oliues bog;
Seue nigt ſiðen euerilc on

row.cell: After seven days the dove left the ark and returned with an olive bough.

cell.p:
He is let ut flegen, crepen, and gon,
wið-uten ilc ſeuend clene der

ðe he ſacrede on an aucter.
Sex hundred ger and on dan[113] olde

row.cell: Seven nights after all are let out of the ark.

cell.p:
Noe ſag ut of ðe arche-wolde;
ðe firſt moned[112] and te firſt dai,

He ſag erðe drie & te water awai;
get he waſ wiſ and nogt to rad,

row.cell: Noah looked out of the ark and saw that the earth was dry.

cell.p:
Gede he nogt ut, til god him bad.
Ðe toðer moneð was in cumen,

And ſeuene and twenti dais numen,
ðo herde Noe wol bliðe bode

row.cell: Yet went he not out till he was bidden by God.

cell.p:
Of a ſteuene, ðe cam fro gode;
He and hiſe wif wenten ut fre,
Hiſe ſunes and here wifes ðre;

row.cell: At God's command he and his family left the ark.

He made an aucter on godeſ name,
And ſacrede he ðor-on, for ſowleſ frame,
Noah made an altar and sacrificed thereon.

cell.p: Ilc ſeuende der of clene kin,
ðe waſ holden in arche wið-hin,

row.cell:
[Fol. 13.]
The seventh deer was offered up,

div.head: THE RAINBOW APPEARS IN THE WELKIN.

row.cell:
And leten ðe oðre to liue gon,
of hem ben tudered manigon.
the others were allowed to escape alive.

cell.p: Often he [bad] wid[114] frigti bede,

ðat ſwiulc wreche ſo god ðo dede
Ne ſulde more on werlde cumen,
Quat wreche ſo ðor wurðe numen.

row.cell: Noah besought God that he would no more send such destruction upon mankind.

cell.p: God gat it a token of luuen,
Taunede him in ðe wa[l]kene a-buuen

row.cell: God granted his request, and shewed him the rain-bow as a token of His love.
Rein-bowe, men cleped[115] reed and blo;
The rain-bow is called red and blue.

ðe blo tokeneð de[116] wateres wo,
ðat iſ wið-uten and is gon;
The blue denotes the water that drowned all flesh.

cell.p:
ðe rede wid-innen[117] toknet on
wreche ðat ſal get wurðen ſent,
wan al ðis werld wurðe brent;
And al-ſo hege ðe lowe ſal gon,

row.cell: The red betokeneth the destruction of the world by fire.

cell.p: Of[118] noe ſiðen an iſ ðre ſunen,
ben boren alle ðe in werlde wunen,

row.cell: From Noah and his three sons all mankind have come.

cell.p: Of his kin bi hiſ liue dai;

row.cell: Before his death his family were widely spread.

cell.p:
vten childre and vten wimmen,
wel fowre and .xx. ðhuſent men
woren ſtalwurði boren bi tale,

row.cell:
[Fol. 13b.]
They numbered, excluding women and children, 24,000 stalworth men.

cell.p: Nembrot gat hiſe feres red,

row.cell: Nimrod had dread of water, so he advised his followers to make a tower high and strong.
Twelwe and ſexti men woren ðor-to,
Seventy-two men were employed about it.

div.head: CONFUSION OF TONGUES. ORIGIN OF IDOLATRY.

cell.p: Meiſter men for to maken it ſo.

row.cell: Al waſ on ſpeche ðor bi-foren,
All spoke one speech before.

cell.p:
ðor woren ſundri ſpeches boren;
ðo wurðen he frigti and a-griſen,
for dor[119] waſ ſundri ſpecheſ riſen,

row.cell: Now sundry tongues arose and sorely terrified the workmen.

Sexti lond-ſpeches and .xii. mo,
weren delt ðane in werlde ðo.
Seventy-two land-speeches were then spoken.
Babel, ðat tur, bi-lef un-mad,
That tower was called Babel.
The folk became scattered afar upon the earth.

cell.p: Beluſ king waſ nembrot ſune,

row.cell: Belus was Nimrod's son, and after him reigned Nilus, who set up an image in remembrance of his father.

cell.p: After hiſ fader, and he ſo dede,
He it ſetten on an mirie ſtede;
He boren ðat likneſſe wurðing,

row.cell: Nilus rewarded all that honoured this likeness.

Calden it bel, after belum;
After ðis cam ſwilc oðer ſum,
They called it Bel, after Belum.

cell.p: Manie man, iſ frend for to munen,
Made likneſſe after ðe wunen,

row.cell: Many made likenesses of their friends.
Bel was the first, and hence the names Bal or Balim.

cell.p: Ydolatrie ðuſ waſ boren,

for quuam mani man iſ for-loren.
Of ſem, and of ðe folc ðe of him cam,
luue and dred under gode nam;
Of ðis kinge wil we leden ſong,

row.cell: Thus was idolatry introduced, by which many are destroyed.

cell.p: Cristes helpe be us amonge!

Noe, ſem, arfaxath, ſale,
Heber, phaleth, ðe ſexte iſ he,
Reu, ſaruch, nacor, thare,
ðiſ iſ ðe tende fro noe.

row.cell: The family of Shem.

Ðis oðer werldes elde iſ ſo,
A ðhuſent ger ſeuenti and two.
[Fol. 14b.]

cell.p: ðe ðridde werldeſ elde cam,

row.cell: The third age of the world began when Terah begat Abram.

cell.p: Aram bi-gat loth, and ſarray,
And melcham, and waſ ſort leui

row.cell: Haran begat Lot and Sarai and Milcah.

In lond caldea, hur hicte ðe tun,
Quor deades ſtrenge warp him dun;
They dwelt in Ur of the Chaldees.

cell.p: ðor fader, and breðere, and childre, and wif,

Him bi-ſtoden wið ſorwes ſtrif;
ðo ðogte thare on hiſ mod,

row.cell: Much strife was there between father and brother, children and wife.

cell.p:
long bigging iſ here nogt god.
Nachor he gaf wif melcam,
And trewe ſarray abram.

row.cell: Terah did not care to remain long in this town.

cell.p: He waſ hiſe neve, wol wel he dede.

row.cell: Abram having no children adopted Lot as his son.

cell.p:
Thare let hur, and ðeðen he nam,
And wulde to lond canahan,
Cam into a burgt[121] ðat het aram,
In londe meſopothaniam.

row.cell: Terah left Ur and came to Haran in Mesopotamia.

Wið him ledde he nachor, melcam,
Sarray, loth, and abram.
With him he took his sons and daughters.
Tho[122] hundred ger and fifue mo,
Terah died when he was two hundred and five years old.
Thare lið biried in aram.
He lies buried in Haran.

div.head: ABRAM REACHES CANAAN. HE GOES TO EGYPT.

cell.p: God ſeide wurd to abram:—

"Abram, ðu fare ut of lond and kin
To a lond ic ðe ſal bringen hin."
Sex ger and fiftene mo,
Adde Abram on iſ elde ðo.

row.cell: God then commanded Abram to leave Haran.

Abram tok loth wið ſarray,
Hiſe agte, and erue he ledde him bi,
For in to lond cananeam,
He departed, taking with him Lot and Sarai.
First he came to Sichem,

cell.p: ðer-fore it higte pentapolis,

Of weledeſ[123] fulſum and of bliſ,
Nov iſt a water of loðlic ble,

row.cell: and afterwards to Pentapolis (the five cities of the plain),

cell.p:
Men callið it ðe dede ſe;
Ilc ðing deieð ðor-inne iſ driuen;
Ne may no fiſ ðor-inne liuen;

row.cell: where now stands the Dead Sea.

cell.p: ſal cumen in to iſ kinneſ hond."

row.cell: The cities were destroyed for man's sin.

ðor god him taunede, made habram
An alter, and fro ðeðen he nam.
[Fol. 15b.]

cell.p: An oðer alter abram ſeli
Made bi-twen betel and ai.

row.cell: Abram raised an altar between Bethel and Ai.

At damaſke iſ ðe ðridde ſtede,
Quer abram iſ bigging dede,
And ðeden for he, for hunger bond,
Damascus was the third place where Abram dwelt.

cell.p:
feger ut in to egipte lond;
ðor he ſeide ðat ſarrai

row.cell: Famine drove him to Egypt.

cell.p:
waſ hiſ ſiſter, al for-ði
for he dredde him to leten iſ lif
If he wiſten ghe wore iſ wif;

row.cell: To save his life he said that Sarai was his sister.
Sarai was fair and Egypt's folk were lecherous.

div.head: PHARAOH TAKES AWAY SARAI, AND IS PUNISHED BY A PLAGUE.

row.cell: Soon was Sarai taken from Abram, and brought to king Pharaoh.

cell.p: God ſente on him ſekeneſſe & care,

And lettede al his lecher-fare.
Sarray liuede in clene lif,

row.cell: God plagued the king with sickness.

cell.p:
And ðe king ðholede ſorges ſtrif
Til he wiſte al ðat ſtrif
Cam him on for abram wif;

row.cell: Pharaoh at last became aware that all this strife was on account of Sarai,

ðo ſente he after abram,
And bi-tagte he him iſ leman,
so he restored her to her husband,

cell.p: And gaf him lond, and agte, and fe,

And leue, ðor quiles his wille be,
To wune egipte folc among,
And friðen him wel fro euerilc wrong,
Bad him to god hiſ erdne beren,

row.cell:
[Fol. 16.]
and gave Abram land and cattle.

cell.p:
ðat ywel him ſulde nunmor deren.
ðor wunede abram in welðe and in frið,

row.cell: In Egypt the patriarch abode in security.

cell.p:
Egipte clerkes woren him wið,
And hem lerede, witterlike,

Aſtronomige and arſmetike;
He was hem lef, he woren him hold.

row.cell: Egypt's clerks held him in high honour.

cell.p:
God gaf him ðor ſiluer and gold,
And hird, and orf, and ſrud, and ſat,
Vn-achteled welðe he ðor bi-gat.

row.cell: God greatly increased his riches.

cell.p:
bileften bi-twen betel and ay,
ðor he quilum her wiſten wunen,
Or he weren to egipte cumen.

row.cell: Out of Egypt Abram went to Canaan, and abode between Bethel and Ai.

cell.p: So wex here erue, and ſo gan ðen
An twen here hirdeſ ſtriuing gan ben;

row.cell: Strife arose between Abram and Lot's herdsmen.

Loth him cheſ, bi leue of abram,
ðat herðe hende ðe flum iurdan;
Lot, by leave of his uncle, chose the plains of the

div.p: w in MS. But the w is much like p.

div.head: ABRAM DWELLS AT MAMRE. LOT IN SODOM.

cell.p: In mirie dale hiſe bigginge he ches,
ðat he ſiðen twie for-les.

row.cell: Jordan for his dwelling-place.
Abram let loth in welðe and wale,
[Fol. 16b.]

cell.p:
And ferde a-wei to mambre dale;
ðor wunede abram henden ebron,
ðat burge an oðer man lið on,

row.cell: Abram dwelt in Mamre-dale, towards Ebron.
This city is called Kirjatharba, i. e. four cities.

cell.p: for ðat fowre biried ðor ben;

row.cell: Four lie buried there.

cell.p: And iacob and hiſe wif lia.

row.cell: There was laid Adam and Eve, Abram and Sarai, Jacob and Leah.

cell.p:
And abram woren he breðre ſworen.
Quor abram wunede, ðor wex bi
An ok' ðat waſ of gibi,

row.cell: Mamre, Eschol, and Aner were sworn brothers with Abram.

cell.p: ðer het god abre ðat tagte lond

row.cell: God promised that Abram's seed should possess the land wherein he was a stranger.

cell.p: Ðo wurðen waxen ſo wide and ſpred,
pride and giſcinge of louerd-hed;

row.cell: Then was pride widely spread, and desire of sovereignty.

Neg ilc burge hadde iſe louereding,
Sum waſ king, and ſum kumeling;
Nearly every city had its ruler.

cell.p: Sum waſ wið migte[125] ſo forð gon,
ðat hadden he under hem mani on.

Fif burges of pentapoliſ,
Adama, bala, Seboyſ,
And ſodoma wið gomorra,
ðe kinges welten burges ðoa,

row.cell: The five cities of Pentapolis, ruled over by their own kings,

div.p: The MS. has migt; but migte is at the bottom of p. 16 b in the catchwords—"Sū waſ wið migte."

div.head: THE BATTLE OF FOUR KINGS AGAINST FIVE.

row.cell:
On-kumen was cadalamor,
king of elam, wið ferding ſtor;
were conquered by Chedorlaomer, and paid him tribute.

cell.p: .xij. ger he weren under iſ hond,
And gouen him gouel of here lond;

row.cell: Twelve years they were under his hand.

.xiij. ger gan ſo forð gon
wulde he giuen him gouel non;
In the thirteenth they rebelled,

cell.p: ðre kinges haued he wið him brogt,

row.cell: Chedorlaomer and other three kings made war upon the cities.

cell.p: fowre on-ſeken and fifue weren,

row.cell: Much sorrow they wrought. The four kings conquered the five.

cell.p: ðe fifwe up to ðe dunes flen,

ðe fowre in to ðe tuneſ ten;
wifwes, and childre, and agte, and ſrud,

row.cell: The five flee to the hills, and the four to the cities of the plain.

cell.p:
He ledden a-wei wið herte prud.
Loth and iſ agte, childre and wif,
ben led a-wei bunden wið ſtrif;

row.cell: They led away with them Lot, his goods, children, and wife.
oc on of hem, ðe flogen a-wei
[Fol. 17b.]

cell.p:
Told it abram ðat ilke deai.
ðre hundred men and .xiij. wigt,

Alle ſtalwurði and witter of figt,
wið mambre, and excol, and anel,
Abram let him tunde wel;
ðat hird he folged[126] alſ to ðan,

row.cell: But one escaped and told Abram, who armed 313 servants and pursued the enemy.

cell.p: He woren drunken and ſlepi,

Abram[127] folc made hem dredi;
ſo heg, ſo long, ne ſpared hem nogt,

row.cell: Abram found them drunk and sleepy.

Alle he ben ðor to gronde brogt,
wið-ðuten ðo ðe cuden flen;
He brought them all to ground.

div.p: An is is inserted by a later hand.

div.head: ABRAM RESCUES LOT. MELCHIZEDEK BLESSES HIM.

cell.p: get ne migten he ſiker ben,
Abram hem folwede and wrogte woa;

row.cell: He pursued them unto Hoba, near Damascus.

cell.p: wenden hom to here ogen ſtede,

row.cell: Much spoil he took.

for loteſ luue fel him ðuſ rigt,
Borwen he ben wel of dat[129] figt.
All this he did for love of Lot.

cell.p: Sodomes king in kinge dale,

Mette abram wið feres wale,
In ðe weie ðe ligið to ſalem,
ðe ſiðen iſ cald ieruſalem.

row.cell:
[Fol. 18.]
The king of Sodom went out to meet Abram.

cell.p: Melchiſedech, ſalameſ king,

row.cell: Melchizedek brought him bread and wine.

cell.p: Habram gaf him ðe tigðe del

row.cell: Abram gave him a tenth of the spoil.

cell.p: for he waſ boðen king and preſt,
of elde moſt, of wit hegest;

row.cell: Melchizedek was both priest and king.

wiſte no man of werlðe ðo,
Quat kinde he waſ kumen fro;
None knew from what family he sprung.

cell.p: Oc ſumme ſeiden ðat it waſ ſem,

ðiſ preſt and [oc] king of ſalem,
or or ðe flod waſ long bi-forn
of noe bi-geten, of[131] iſ wif born,

row.cell: Some said that this king of Salem was Shem,

cell.p: And fro ſo longe ðor bi-foren
Liuede til yſaac waſ boren.

row.cell: who lived until the birth of Isaac.

Sodomes king bed dor[132] abram
Al agte and erf, wið-uten man,[133]
Alle heſ hadde wið migte bi-geten,
The king of Sodom offered Abram the goods and cattle taken from the enemy.

div.head: ABRAM COMPLAINS FOR WANT OF AN HEIR.

cell.p: wolde he nogt him hiſ ſwinc for-geten,

row.cell:
oc abram dede ðor meðelike wel,
wid-held he ðor-of neu[er]e on del,
oc al ðat euere fel him to,

[Fol. 18b.]
The patriarch would accept of nothing.

cell.p:
Sac-les he let hin welden it ſo.
Ebruiſ ſeigen, wune hem wex her
To algen ilk fiftene ger,
for loth waſ fifti winter hold,
Quan abram him bi-told.

row.cell: Then first began the custom of keeping the 15th year holy.
Abel primiceſ firſt bi-gan,
Abel first began first-fruit.

cell.p:
And decimas first abram;
Nu iſt ſo boden and ſo bitagt,
Quo-ſo hiſ alt him bi agt.

row.cell: Abram tithes.

cell.p:
After ðiſ ſpac god to abram:—
"ðin berg and tin werger ic ham.
ðin ſwinc ðe ſal ben gulden wel,
wid[134] michel welðe in good[e] ſel."

row.cell: After this God spake to Abram, saying, "I am thy safety and thy defence, thy toil shall be requited."

cell.p: In al min welðe ſal he wunen?"

row.cell: Quoth Abram, "What avails wealth, seeing that I am childless, and that Eliezer's son shall inherit my wealth?"

cell.p:
Quat god, "ſo ſal it nogt ben,
Of ðe ſelf ſal ðin erward ten."
Abram leuede ðiſ hot in ſped,
dat[135] waſ him [told] to rigt-wiſhed.

row.cell: God said, "Of thyself shall thine heir come."

ðre der he toc, ilc ðre ger hold,
And ſacrede god on an wold;
Abram took three deer each three years old and offered them as a sacrifice.
of godeſ bode he nam god kep,
An heifer, a goat, and a sheep he took, and divided them in two and set them apart.

cell.p:
And ðor a duue and a turtul ok
Sat up on-rum til heuene he tok,
And of ðo doles kep he nam

row.cell: The dove and the turtle he divided not.
Gredi foueles fellen ðor-on,
Greedy fowls fell upon the carcases.

div.head: SARAI BEING BARREN GIVES HAGAR TO ABRAM.

cell.p: ðat ðogte abram wel iwel don,

row.cell:
kagte iſ wei, quan it waſ nigt,
ðo cam on him vgging and frigt;
Abram drove them away. Then came on him fear and fright.

cell.p: A michel fier he ſag, and an brigt,
gliden ðor twen ðo doles rigt.

row.cell: A great and bright fire he saw glide down between the pieces.

cell.p:
God ſeide him ðor a ſoðe drem
ðe timinge of iſ beren-tem,
And hu he ſulde in pine ben,

And uten erdes ſorge ſen;
fowre hundred ger ſulden ben gon,

row.cell: In a dream God showed Abram the future condition of his descendants.

cell.p:
Hor he ſulden wel cumen a-gon,
oc ſiðen ſulde in here hond,
bi-cumen ðat hotene lond.

row.cell: Canaan is promised as his inheritance.

ðo wiſte abram wel michel mor
Quat waſ to cumen ðan he wiſte or.
Then knew Abram much more of what was to come than he ever knew before.

cell.p: Siðen bi-fel ðat ſarrai,
for ghe waſ longe untuderi,

row.cell: Sarai, being barren, gives Hagar to Abram.
[Fol. 19b.]
Hagar having conceived, despised her mistress.

cell.p: Ghe held hire hard in ðralleſ wune,
And dede hire ſorge and anger mune;

row.cell: Sarai afflicts her thrall.

cell.p:
ðo fleg agar fro ſarray,
wimman wið childe, one and ſori,
In ðe diſerd, wil and weri,

And an angel cam ðor hire bi,
wiſte hire drogen ſori for ðriſt,

row.cell: Hagar flees from Sarai into the desert homeless and weary.

cell.p:
At a welle quemede hire liſt,
And bad hire ſone wenden agen,
And to hire leuedi buxum ben;

row.cell: An angel commands her to return and be buxom to her lady.

And ſeide ghe ſulde ſunen wel
And timen, and clepen it ſmael,[136]
He tells her of her child.

div.head: ISHMAEL IS BORN. CIRCUMCISION IS INSTITUTED.

cell.p: And he ſulde ben man migti,
And of him kumen folc frigti;

row.cell:
Ghe wente agen, and bar ðat child,
And abram wurð wið hire milde.
Hagar returns, and Ishmael is born.

cell.p: lxxx. gere and ſexe mo

Hadde abram on hiſ elde ðo,
And .xiii. ger ðor after told,

row.cell: Abram was then fourscore and six years old.
ix. and nigneti[137] ger he waſ old,
When Abram was ninety-nine years old God changed his name to Abraham.

cell.p: Quuanne him cam bode in ſunder run,

fro gode of circumcicioun.
His name ðo wurð a lettre mor,
Hiſ wiueſ leſſe ðan it waſ or,
for ðo wurd abram abraham,

row.cell: Sarai's name is also changed to Sarah.

cell.p: He him ſelf wurð ðanne circumciſ,

row.cell: Circumcision is instituted.

cell.p: Quuo ne bar ðanne iſ merk him on
fro godes folc ſulde he be don.

row.cell: Whoso bore not this mark upon him was to be cut off from God's folk.

cell.p:
Abraham he broghten wel bliðe bode.
Abraham he[m] ran wel ſwiðe agon,

row.cell: Afterwards in the dale of Mamre Abraham saw figures three, seemly messengers from God.

cell.p:
And of ðe ðre he wurðede ðe ton,
ðe god him dede in herte ſen,
ðe waſ wurði wurðed to ben;

row.cell: Abraham entertains the angels.

bred, kalueſ fleiſ, and flures bred,
And buttere, hem ðo sondes bed;
He set before them calves flesh, bread and flour and butter.

cell.p: for ðat he bad wið herte fre,
He it nomen in charite;

row.cell: What he offered with a free heart his guests took in charity,

So malt ðat mete in hem to nogt,
So a watreſ drope in a fier brogt.

[Fol. 20b.]
though it was but as a drop of water in a fire.

cell.p: Abraham ſtod and quamede hem wel,
Hiſ good[e] wil was hem good mel.
ðat ge ſal of a ſune trimen."

row.cell: Abraham is promised a son.

cell.p: Abraham on wane of an hundred told;

row.cell: Sarah heard the words of the Lord.

Ghe glente and ðhogte, migte it nogt ben,
And ghe ðat ſulde her wið childe be ſen;
She did not believe them.

cell.p: And Abraham trewid it ful wel,
And it wurð ſoð binnen ſwilc ſel.

row.cell: Abraham, however, trowed it full well.
Then the three went towards Sodom.
The destruction of Sodom is revealed to Abraham.

cell.p: ðo adde abram iſ herte ſor,
for loth hiſ newe wunede ðor.

row.cell: He is in great grief on account of Lot.

"Louerd," quad he, "hu ſaltu don,
If ðu ſalt nimen wreche ðor on;
He intercedes for the wicked cities.

cell.p: Salt ðu nogt ðe rigt-wiſe weren,
Or for hem ðe toðere með beren?"

row.cell:
Quad god, "find ic ðor ten or mo,
Ic ſal meðen ðe ſtede for ðo."
Durſte Abraham freinen nunmor,
God promises to spare the cities for the sake of five righteous.
Abraham departs sore at heart.

cell.p: Sunne iſ weſt under erðe numen,
Quuanne he ben to ſodome cumen;

row.cell: At even two angels came to Sodom.

Get ſat loth at ðe burges gate,
After ſum geſte ſtod him quake;[138]
Lot sat at the city's gate, and seeing them,
He roſ, and lutte, and ſcroð him wel,

cell.p:
And bead hem hom to iſ oſtel
To herbergen wið him ðat nigt,
ðo ſwete angeles, faier and brigt;
And he ſo deden alſ he hem bead,
He wiſten him bergen fro ðe dead;

row.cell: he invited them to his home to stay with him that night.

cell.p:
And loth hem ſerued faire and wel,
And he him gulden it euerilc del.
Oc al ðat burgt folc ðat helde waſ on,
ðe migte lecher crafte don,

row.cell: Lot served his guests fair and well.

To lothes huſ he cumen ðat nigt
And bi-ſetten it redi to figt;
The wicked Sodomites beset Lot's house.

cell.p: He boden him bringen ut o-non,
ðo men ðat woren ðidir in-gon.

row.cell: They bade him bring out the strangers.

[Fol. 21b.]
Lot offered them his daughters.

cell.p:
for wicke and feble waſ here ðogt.
ðat folc vn-ſeli, ſinne wod,
ðo ſori wrecches of yuel blod
wulden him ðor gret ſtrengðe don,
Til wreche and letting cam hem on.

row.cell: The wicked folk sought to harm Lot.

ðis angels two drogen loth in,
And ſhetten to ðe dure-pin.
The angels drew Lot in.

cell.p: Wil ſiðen cam on euerilc on,

ðo wrecches ðe wið-vten gon,
for al ðat nigt he ſogten ðor

row.cell: Blindness came upon the Sodomites,

ðe dure, and fundend[139] neuere mor.
ðo ſeiden ðiſ angeles to loth wið ſped,
and they sought the door in vain.

cell.p:
If ðu frend haueſt and wi[l]t don red,
Bid him, or day, redi ben,
And ſwiðe ut ðiſ burgeſ flen,
elles ſulen he brennen and for-faren,

If he ne bi time heðe[n] waren.
Two ðor werren quam him ðogte ear
To wedden hiſ two dogtres ðear;[140]

row.cell: Lot is commanded to leave the city with his friends before daybreak.

div.head: THE DESTRUCTION OF SODOM AND GOMORRAH.

cell.p: Loth hem warnede, wiſlike and wel,
Oc he ne troweden him neuere a del.

row.cell: Lot warned his sons-in-law in vain.

On morgen quan day cam hem to,
Loth and hiſ dogtres two
The angels led Lot and his family out of Sodom,
Ledden ðiſ angeles ut in ſel,

cell.p:
And boden hem and tagten wel,
ðat here non wente agen,
for non ðhing he migte ſen.

row.cell: and bade them turn not back.

cell.p: Loth waſ wanſum, and ðugte long
vp to ðo dunes ðe weie hard and ſtrong;

row.cell: Lot thought the way to the hills hard and strong.

cell.p:
"Louerd," quat he, "gunde under dun,
mot hic ben borgen in ðat tun!"
ðo angeles ſeiden, "we ſulen it ſren,[141]
ðor quile ðu wilt ðor-inne ben;

row.cell: He intreated that he might dwell in Segor.

Ai waſ borgen bala-ſegor
ðor quile ðat loth dwelledde ðor;
This city was safe while Lot abode there;

cell.p: Oc ſiðen loth wente ut of hine,

brende it ðhunder, ſanc it erðe-dine.
Sone ſo loth ut of ſodome cam,

row.cell: when he left it, it was destroyed.

cell.p:
brend-fier-rein ðe burge bi-nam;
Hardere wreche ðor waſ cumen
ðan ear was vnder flode numen;

row.cell: Sodom was destroyed by fire,
for sin and "unkind deeds."

cell.p: Ðo lotes wif wente hire a-gon,
Sone ghe ſtod, wente in to a ſton;

row.cell: Lot's wife turned back, and "went into a stone."

cell.p:
So iſt nu forwent mirie dale
In to dririhed and in to bale,
ðe ſwarte flum, ðe dede ſe,

Non fiſ, non fuel ðor-inne mai be.
ðat water iſ ſo deades driuen,

row.cell:
[Fol. 22b.]
Thus is this merry dale turned into a swarthy lake.
Non ðing ne mai ðor-inne liuen;
Nothing may live therein.

div.head: THE BIRTHS OF AMMON AND MOAB.

row.cell: Men ſeið ðe treen ðat ðor henden ben

cell.p:
Waxen in time, and brimen, and ðen,
Oc quane here apples ripe ben,

row.cell: Trees on its banks produce apples,

cell.p:
fier-iſles man mai ðor-inne ſen;
ðat erd iſ oten ſaltes dale,
Maniman ðor-of holdet litel tale.

row.cell: which contain ashes only.
Lot soon left Segor.
For fear he fled to the hills, and dwelt in a cave.

cell.p: ðo meidenes herden quilum ſeien,

ðat fier ſulde al ðis werld forſweðen,
And wenden wel ðat it were cumen,
And fiereſ wreche on werld numen,
And ðat man-kinde wore al for-loren
but of hem ðre wore man boren.

row.cell: Lot's daughters thought all mankind had perished, and that, unless they had children, the world would come to an end.

ðis maidenes redden ſone[142] on-on
Quat hem two wore beſt to don,
They consulted as to what was best to be done.
Hu he migten vnder-gon

cell.p:
Here fader, ðat he ne[143] wore ðor gon;
Wið wineſ drinc he wenten iſ ðhogt,
So ðat he haueð ðe dede wrogt,
And on eiðer here a knaue bi-geten,

ðiſ ne mai nogt ben for-geten.
ðiſ maidenes deden it in god dhogt,[144]
ðe fader oc drunken ne wiſte he it nogt.

row.cell: They made their father drunk so that he wrought the deed, and each begot a child.

cell.p: ðe firſte him bar moab ðat ſune,

row.cell: The first bore Moab, the other Ammon.

cell.p: NV bi-oueð uſ to wenden a-gen,
And of abraham ſong under-gon.

row.cell: Now turn we to Abraham.

Abraham up on morgen ſtod,
Wið reuli lote and frigti mod;
On the morrow he looked toward Sodom,

cell.p: To-ward ſodome he ſag ðe roke
And ðe brinfires ſtinken[145] ſmoke,

row.cell: and saw that the city had been destroyed.

And wente a-wei fro mambre dale,
So ſore him reu of ðat bale.
For sorrow he left Mamre's dale

cell.p: Suðen he wente & wunede in geraris,
bi-twen cade and vr, y-wis;

row.cell: and went and abode in Gerar.

cell.p:
ðor he ſeide eft, for luue of lif,
ðat ſiſter wore ſarra his wif.
Quilum of[146] er [147]pharraon hire toc,
Nu takeð abimalech hire oc;

row.cell: There he said Sarah was his sister.

Sene it was ðat ghe waſ fair wif,
Quan ghe waſ luued in ſo long lif.
Abimalech wurð ſek on-on,

[Fol. 23b.]
Abimelech took her to wife.

cell.p:
And oðer wreche iſ folc cam on;
Nogt wif-kinnes non birðe ne nam,
ðor quiles he ðor wið-helð ſaram.
On dreme him cam tiding for-quat

row.cell: Sickness fell on him and on his folk.

cell.p: And ſente after abraham ðat ilc ſel,

row.cell: The cause of this evil was made known to him in a dream.

And bi-tagte him hiſ wif a-non,
And hiſ yuel ſort[148] waſ ouer-gon.
He sent back Sarah,

cell.p: His wif and oðere birðe beren,

row.cell: his wife and others bore children, and the quinsy no more troubled him.

cell.p: A ðhuſant plates of ſiluer god

Gaf he ſarra ðat faire blod,
Bad hire ðor hir wið[149] heuod ben hid,
for ſwilc timing was hire bi-tid.
Ðo wulde god bi-ſewen ſo

of olde abraham and o ſarra ſo.
Ghe wurd wið child, on elde wac,

row.cell: Plates of silver he gave to Sarah.
And trimede and cleped it yſaac.
The birth of Isaac.

div.head: THE BANISHMENT OF HAGAR AND ISHMAEL.

row.cell: ðe egtende dai ðat he waſ boren,

cell.p:
Circumciſed he waſ, a-buten ſchoren;
ðor-of holden ðe ieuwes lay,
Circumciſed on ðe egtende day.
Arabit folc of yſmael,

row.cell: He was circumcised on the eighth day,
which custom the Jews follow.

cell.p: Ðre ger woren yſaac on,

Quane he waſ fro teding don;
Michel geſtninge made abraham
Quane he ðat ſune to borde nam.
Wintres forð-wexen on yſaac,

row.cell: When Isaac was three years old Abraham made a great feast.
Ishmael often mocked Isaac,

cell.p: Sarra waſ ðor-fore often wroð,
Hir waſ yſmaeles anger loð;

row.cell: which caused Sarah to be very wroth.

cell.p:
Ghe bi-mente hire to abraham,
And ſumdel ligtlike he it nam
Til god him bad iſ wiues tale

row.cell: She complains to Abraham.

cell.p: He flemede agar and yſmael
In ſumertid, In egeſt ſel;

row.cell: Abraham banishes Hagar and her son.

Bred, and a fetles wið water fild,
Bar agar wið hire and wið ðe child;
[Fol. 24b.]

cell.p: Bi ðe deſert a-wei che nam,

In ard weie and hete gram;
Wið ſwinc and hete hem wexon ðriſt,

row.cell: By the desert they took their way.

ðe water ſleckede ðe childeſ liſt;
Tid-like hem gan ðat water laken,
They became very thirsty.
The water in the bottle became spent.

cell.p: Ghe leide ðe child under a tre,

row.cell: Hagar placed her child under a tree,
ðor ſat hiſ moder in ſik and ſor,
and sat as far as a bow-shot off.

cell.p:
wende ghe it coueren neuere mor.
Goddeſ merci dede hire reed,

row.cell: She thought it could not recover.

cell.p:
An angel meðede hire ðat ned,
Tagte hire ðor a welle ſpring,
ðat waſ hire ðor ſeli timing;

row.cell: An angel showed her a well-spring,

ðor ghe gan fremen yſmael
Wið watreſ drinc and bredeſ mel,
and she gave the lad drink and bread.

cell.p: filt hire feteleſ, and nam fro ðan
forð to ðe deſert of [150]pharan;

row.cell: Forth they went and dwelt in Paran.

ðor wunede yſmael and agar.
Ghe cheſ him a wif ðe childre bar;
Ishmael married an Egyptian woman.

cell.p: .xii. ſuneſ he auede bi hiſ wif,

Of him cam kinde mikil and rif.
Nabachot waſ hiſ firſt ſune,

row.cell:
[Fol. 25.]
Twelve sons he had, of whom sprang great nations.

cell.p:
In arabie hiſ kinde wune
fro ðe riche flod eufrate,
Wid and fer to ðe rede ſe;

row.cell: In Arabia they dwelt.

Of hiſ oðer ſune cedar,
A ku[n]griche hiſ name bar;
Kedar gave name to a kingdom.

cell.p: And of duma hiſ ſexte ſune,

A ku[n]gdom dirima ðu mune;
Hiſ .ix. waſ tema for-ðan,

row.cell: From Dumah came the kingdom of Dirima.

cell.p:
Iſ ðor a ku[n]glond teman;
And .xii. of ðe cedima,

Het a guglond[151] eſten fro ða.
Flemd waſ agar and yſmael,
and yſaac wex and ðehg wol wel.

row.cell: Teman gets its name from Tema.

cell.p: Abimalech ſag abraham,

Hu welðe him wex and migte cam,
He bad him maken ſiker pligt
Of luue and trewðe, in frendeſ rigt,

row.cell: Abimelech makes a covenant with Abraham,

div.head: AND GIVES HIM THE WELL OF BEERSHEBA.

cell.p: ðat ne ſulde him nogwer deren,
Oc him and hiſe helpen and weren;
ðat here neiðer ſal don oðer un-rigt.

row.cell: and gives him the well of Beersheba.

Abraham gan ðor longe ben,
And tillede corn and ſette treen,
[Fol. 25b.]

cell.p: ðog [it] waſ nogt iſ kinde lond;

Richere he it leet ðan he it fond.
Iff ioſephus ne legeð me,
ðor quiles he wunede in berſabe,

row.cell: Abraham left the land much richer than he found it.

cell.p: ſo waſ yſaaceſ eld told
xx. and fiwe winter old;

row.cell: When Isaac was twenty-five years old,

ðo herde abraham ſteuene fro gode,
Newe tiding, and ſelkuð bode:—
God's word came to Abraham,—

cell.p: "Tac ðin ſune yſaac in hond,
And far wið him to ſiðhingeſ lond,

row.cell: "Take Isaac thy son,

cell.p:
And ðor ðu ſalt him offren me
On an hil ðor ic ſal taunen ðe."
fro berſabe iurneſ two
Waſ ðat lond ðat he bed him two;[152]

row.cell: and offer him on a hill that I shall show thee."

And morie, men ſeið, waſ ðat hil,
ðat god him tawne[de] in his wil;
Moriah that hill was called.

cell.p: Men ſeið ðat dune-iſ ſiðen on

Was mad temple ſalamon,
And ðe auter mad on ðat ſtede
ðor abraham he[153] offrande dede.

row.cell: Upon this hill was afterwards built Solomon's temple.

cell.p: Abraham waſ buxum o rigt,

row.cell: Abraham was obedient to God's commands.

cell.p: ðan he cam dun to ðo duneſ fot,

Non of hiſ men forðere ne mot,
But yſaac iſ dere childe,

row.cell:
[Fol. 26.]
He came to the hill and sent his servants away.
He bar ðe wude wið herte mild,
Isaac bare the wood,

cell.p: And abraham ðe fier and ðe ſwerd bar;

row.cell: and Abraham the fire and the sword.

cell.p: "fader," quað he, "quar ſal ben taken
ðe offrende ðat ðu wilt maken?"

row.cell: "Where," quoth Isaac, "is the offering that thou wilt make?"

Quat abraham, "god ſal bi-ſen
Quor-of ðe ofrende ſal ben;
Quoth Abraham, "God will provide the offering.

cell.p: Sellik ðu art on wer[l]de cumen,

row.cell: In a wonderful manner thou camest into the world, and so shalt thou depart hence.

cell.p: And of ðe seluen holocaustum hauen,
ðanc it him ðat he it wulde crauen."

row.cell: God requires thee as an offering."

cell.p:
Yſaac waſ redi mildelike,
Quan ðat he it wiſte witterlike.
Oc abraham it wulde wel
quat-ſo god bad, ðwerted he it neuer a del;

row.cell: Isaac was ready to be sacrificed.

Yſaac waſ leid ðat auter on,
So men ſulden holocauſt don;
Isaac was placed upon the altar.

cell.p: And abraham ðat ſwerd ut-drog,
And waſ redi to ſlon him nuge,[154]

row.cell: Abraham drew out his sword to slay his son, but an angel forbad him to harm the child.

cell.p:
for yſaac bi-leaf un-ſlagen;
Bi-aften bak, aſ he nam kep,

row.cell: [Fol. 26b.]

cell.p:
faſte in ðornes he ſag a ſep,
ðat an angel ðor-inne dede;
It waſ brent on yſaac ſtede.

row.cell: A ram is offered instead of Isaac.

cell.p:
And, or abraham ðeðen for,
God him ðor bi him-ſeluen ſwor
ðat he ſal michil hiſ kinde maken,

row.cell: Ere Abraham departed God swore to him that his seed should inherit the land.

div.head: ELIEZER IS SENT TO MESOPOTAMIA.

cell.p: He wente bliðe and fagen agen,

To berſabe he gunne teen,
Sarra waſ fagen in kindes wune,
ðat [hire][155] bilef ðat dere ſune.

row.cell: Abraham went home joyful and glad.

cell.p: Ðor quiles abraham wunede ðor,

Him cam good tiding of nachor,
ðat melca bar him egte ſunen;

row.cell: While at Beersheba he heard good tidings of Nahor.
Huſ waſ eldeſt, if we rigt munen.
Huz was Nahor's first-born.

cell.p: Rigt-wiſ iob cam of hiſ kin,
Hus lond he waſ riche wid-hin;[156]

row.cell: Job came of his kin.

Of[157] buz, hiſ broðeres kin, cam
Buzites, Eliv, Balaam.
Of Buz came the Buzites, Eliv and Balaam.

cell.p: Abraham, riche of welðe and wale,
wente a-gen in to manbre dale;

row.cell:
[Fol. 27.]
Abraham went again to Mamre.

Sarra ðo ſtarf, an hundred ger old
And ſeuene and .xx. winter told.
Sarah died being 127 years old.

cell.p: Abraham ſente eliezer

to lond meſopotanie fer,
To caram ðor iſ fader lay,
(Or he cam ðor waſ manie day)

row.cell: Abraham sent Eliezer to Mesopotamia,

cell.p: To fechen yſaac hom a wif,
Of hiſ kinde ðe ðor waſ in lif.

row.cell: to fetch a wife for Isaac.
Ten kameles ſemeð[158] forð he nam,
Ten camels he took with him.

cell.p:
Wið michel ſwinc he ðider cam
At a welle wið-uten ðe tun;
ðor he leide hiſe ſemes dun,

row.cell: Eliezer came to a well without the city.

cell.p:
ðor he wulde him reſten and ben,
Sum good tiding heren or ſen.
"Louerd god," quað he mildelike,

"min erdne ðu forðe ſelðhelike,
ðiſ dai me lene hire to ſen,
ðat ſal yſaaces leman ben."

row.cell: He there prayed to God to send him good speed.

cell.p: He bad hiſe bede on good ſel.
Rebecca, bi-geten of batuel,

row.cell: He offered his prayer in a good time.

div.p: MS. hire is written over in the later hand.

row.cell:
Of nachor bi-geten, of melca boren,
Cam to ðat welle ðor him bi-foren,
Rebekah came to that well,

cell.p: And him and ilc-on his kamel
Wið watres drinc ghe quemede wel.

row.cell: and she gave him and his camel water to drink.

Oðere maidenes wið hire cumen,
Ne wor nogt ſo forð ðeuwe numen.
[Fol. 27b.]

cell.p: Eliezer lerede ðor

row.cell: Eliezer learned that she was of the family of Nahor.

cell.p: ðogte he, ðiſ maiden wile ic hauen

And to min louerdes bofte bi-crauen;[159]
for kindes luue he waſ hire hold,

row.cell: Thought he, this maiden will I have as a wife for Isaac.

cell.p:
Wið beges and ringes boðen of gold,
Aſkede here if ghe migte taken

Herberge for hire frendes ſake[n].
Maiden rebecca ðanne ran,
And kiddit to hire broðer laban,

row.cell: He gave her ear-rings and bracelets of gold.

cell.p: And laban cam to ðat welle ner,

faiger welcumede he ðer eliezer,
And[160] fond good grið and good hostel,
Him, and hiſe men, and hiſe kamel.

row.cell: Laban came to the well, invited him home, and entertained him well.

cell.p: Eliezer, or he wulde eten,
Quilc ſelðe and welðhe him wel bi-cam,

row.cell: Eliezer would not eat till he had told his errand;

Sent he waſ ðider, for kinde wune,
After a wif to yſaac hiſ ſune.
how he had been sent by Abraham to seek a wife for Isaac.

cell.p: ſeide he, "rebecca wile ic hauen,
To yſac-iſ bi-ofte wile ic crauen.

row.cell:
Laban and hiſ moder wið-ðan
fagneden wel ðiſ ſondere man;
Laban and the mother were well pleased with the messenger.

cell.p: (Quan god haueð it ſo bi-ſen,
Alſe he ſendet, alſ it ſal ben.)

row.cell:
Wið gold, and ſiluer, and wið ſrud,
ðiſ ſonde made ðe mayden prud;
With gold and silver and raiment Eliezer made the maiden proud.

cell.p: ðe broðer and de[161] moder oc

Riche gifteſ eliezer ðe[162] toc.
Sone o-morwen he gan him garen,

row.cell: Gifts also he gave to the brother and mother.

cell.p:
And crauede hiſ erdene, and wolde hom faren,
for ſcrið, ne mede, ne wold he ðor

Ouer on nigt drechen nunmor;
And ðo gan ðat moder and laban

row.cell: No longer than one night would he delay his errand.

cell.p:
Rebecca freinen ðor for-ðan,
And ghe it grantede mildelike,
And he hire bi-tagten bliðelike.

row.cell: Rebekah's consent was first asked and obtained.

cell.p:
Siðen men hauen holden ſkil,
firſt to freinen ðe wimmaneſ wil,
Or or men hire to louerd giue,
for wedding or for morgen-giwe.

row.cell: For this reason men ask the woman's will before she is given in marriage.

cell.p:
Eliezer iſ went hiſ wei
And haueð hem boden godun dai.
Or he wel homward cumen was,
Yſaac waſ cume to geraſis,

row.cell: Eliezer takes his departure, wishing all a good day.

cell.p:
And wunede ðor in ðogt and care,
for moderes dead and ſondes fare.
In a weie an time he cam,

row.cell:
[Fol. 28b.]
Isaac mourned for the death of his mother.

cell.p: Eððede hiſ ſorge, brogt him a wif

row.cell: Eliezer brought him a wife by whom he was comforted.

cell.p: He luuede hire on-like and wel,
And ſge ne bi-ſpac him neuere a del.

row.cell: Isaac loved Rebekah well, and she never contradicted him.

div.head: THE BIRTH OF ESAU AND JACOB.

row.cell:
Get men seyn[164] ðat abraham,
ſiðen calde agar ceturam,
Men say that Abraham called Hagar Keturah.

cell.p: And ſge bar him ſiðen ſex ſunen;

Abraham dede hem ſiðen ſundri wunen;
fer eſt fro cratonidé,
Weren he ſpred to ðe rede se.
Yſaac he let al hiſ god,
for he waſ bi-geten of kinde blod.

row.cell: She bore him seven sons.

cell.p:
An hundred ger hold and ſeuenti
And .v. he waſ leid ſarram bi.
boðen yſaac and yſmael
Him bi-ſtoden wurlike and wel.

row.cell: Abraham died at the age of 175.

On hundred ger and .xxxvij.
Liuede yſmael and waſ ðor bi.
Ishmael was 137 years old when he died.

cell.p: Yſaac waſ hold .xl. ger

Quanne rebecca cam him ner;
Longe it waſ or ghe him child bar,

row.cell:
[Fol. 29.]
Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife.

cell.p:
And he bad god, quanne he it wurð war,
ðat he ſulde fillen ðat quede

ðat he[165] abraham quilum dede.
ðo wurð rebecca childre bere,

row.cell: Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, who was barren.

cell.p:
ðat ghe felte ful time in gere;
At on burdene ghe under-stod

two ðe weren hire ſibbe blod;
Alſe ðhute hire day and nigt,

row.cell: Rebekah conceived.

Alſe he wrogten and[166] figt,
Queðer here ſulde birðen bi-foren.
The children struggled together within her.

cell.p:
Oc eſau waſ firmeſt boren,
And iacob ſone after, ic wot,
for ðat he heldim bi ðe fot.

row.cell: Esau was the first born, and Jacob was born soon after.

cell.p: Sexti ger yſaac waſ old,

row.cell: Sixty years was Isaac at this time.

div.p: seyn is at the side in a later hand.
In a later hand at the side.

div.head: THE PRIVILEGES OF THE FIRST BORN.

cell.p: Wexen boden yſaac ſunes,
And ðhogen, and adden ſundri wunes;

row.cell: Isaac's sons grew up and had different occupations.

Eſau wilde man huntere,
And Iacob tame man tiliere.
Esau was a hunter, and Jacob a husbandman.

cell.p: ðe fader luuede eſau wel,
for firme birðe & ſwete mel;

row.cell: Isaac loved Esau for that he was the eldest.

ðe moder, iacob for tamehed,
And for ðe ali gaſteſ red.
Iacob An time him ſeð a mete

[Fol. 29b.]
Rebekah loved Jacob because of his peaceful disposition.

cell.p: ðat man callen lentil gete,

row.cell: Jacob sod pottage.

And eſau fro felde cam,
Sag ðis pulment, hunger him nam.
Esau came from the field hungry.

cell.p: "Broðer iacob," quat eſau,

row.cell: "Brother," said he, "give me of this warm meat, for I am weary."

cell.p: "Broðer," quad he, "ſel me ðo wunes,

ðe queðen ben ðe firme ſunes,
ðat ic ðin firme birðehe gete,
If ic ðe fille wið ðiſ mete."

row.cell: Jacob said, "Sell me thy birthright, and I will fill thee with meat."

cell.p: Quad eſau, "ful bliðelike,"
And gafe it him wel ſikerlike.

row.cell: Esau consented full blithely.

cell.p: Waſ wune ben ſcrid ſemelike and wel,

row.cell: The eldest son was highly honoured.

cell.p: ðe gungere[168] ſune geuen ðe bliſcing,

row.cell: At his father's death he had the blessing.

And hauen mete ðan at iſ mel,
More or ðe gungere twinne del;
At meat he had a double portion.

cell.p: And quanne ðe fader were grauen,
two doles of ereward riche auen.

row.cell:
[Fol. 30.]
His inheritance was twice as much as the younger's share.

div.head: JACOB DEFRAUDS ESAU OF THE BLESSING.

cell.p:
An time dede hunger yſaac flen,
And he wulde to egipte then,[169]
Oc god him ſente reed in wis
ðat he bi-lef in geraſis;

row.cell: A famine banished Isaac to Gerar.

cell.p:
ðor he was for hiſ fadreſ luue[n]
Holden wurðelike a wel a-buuen.
An hundred ſo mikel wex hiſ tile,
So may god friðe ðor he wile.

row.cell: For his father's sake he was highly esteemed.

cell.p:
Niðede ðat folk him fel wel
And deden him flitten hiſe oſtel.
At berſabe he wunede beſt,
And ðor wurð wið him trewðe feſt

row.cell: The folk of Gerar envied Isaac, so he left them and went to Beersheba.

Abimalech, and luue ſworen,
So he waſ or iſ fader bi-foren.
And helde gede on yſaac,
Abimelech made a covenant with Isaac.

cell.p:
Wurðede ſighteleſ and elde ſwac;[170]
He bad eſau, hiſ firme ſune,

row.cell: Isaac became old and sightless.

fechin him fode, aſ he waſ wune;
If he toke him ðat he wulde eten,
He sends Esau for venison,

cell.p:
Hiſ ſeli bliſcing ſulde he bi-geten.
Ðor quiles eſau ſogte and ran,

row.cell: and promises him his blessing.

cell.p:
Rebecca iacob reden gan;
Two kides he fette and brogtes hire,
And ghe knew wel ðe faderes kire,[171]

row.cell: Rebekah instructs Jacob how to obtain the blessing.

And made ſwiðe on ſele ðat mete,
ſwilc ghe wiſte he wulde eten;
[Fol. 30b.]

cell.p: Sridde ghe iacob and made him ru

ðor he was bare(.) nu lik eſau;
And he ſeruede hiſ fader wel

row.cell: She made him rough like Esau.

cell.p:
Wið wines drinc and ſeles mel.
Yſaac wende it were eſau,

row.cell: Jacob obtained the blessing from his father.

cell.p: "Heuene dew, and erðeſ fetthed,

Of win and olie fulſum-hed,"
And bad him of hiſ kindes louerd ben,
In welðe and migt wurðinge ðen.
Wel bliðe and fagen was iacob ðo,
for bliſced he wente hiſ fader fro.

row.cell: The dew of heaven, the fatness of the earth, plenty of corn and wine, and the lordship over his brethren.

cell.p:
Quan yſaac it under-nam
ðat eſau to late cam,
And ðat iſ broðer, af-ter boren,

Waſ kumen and hadde iſ bliſcing bi-foren,
Wel ſelkuðlike he wurð for-dred;

row.cell: When Isaac understood that Esau came too late he was seized with great fear.

cell.p:
And in ðat dred hiſ ðogt waſ led
In to ligtneſſe for to ſen
Quow god wulde it ſulde ben.

row.cell: In his dread he saw how God would that it should so be.
ðo ſeide yſaac to eſau,
To Esau thus he spoke:
"ðin broðer iacob waſ her nu,
"Thy brother was here just now, and has taken thy blessing, and he shall be blessed."

cell.p: And toc ðin bliſcing liðer-like,
Or he min firme birðe toc,

row.cell: Esau intreats for one blessing.

cell.p: ðo gan eſau ðengen[173] and ſen

row.cell: Isaac promises him that his dwelling shall be of the fatness of the earth and of the dew of heaven.

cell.p: for ydumea, ðat fulſum lond,
Of lewſe god, was in hiſe hond.

row.cell: Idumea became Esau's inheritance.

cell.p:
Quad eſau, "grot ſal bi-cumen,
And wreche of iacob ſal binumen."
Oc rebecca wiſte ðat ðhogt,
ðat hate waſ in hiſe herte brogt,

row.cell: Esau threatens Jacob.

for-ði ghe iacob warnen gan,
And ſente him to hiſ broðer laban;
Rebekah warns Jacob of his brother's intentions.

cell.p: "be ðu ðer," quat ghe, "til eſau

Eðe moðed [be], ðe wreðed nu,
And ðu ſalt ðe betre ſped,

If it beð bi ðin faderes red."
Quad rebecca to hire were,
"Eſau wifuede uſ to dere

row.cell: Rebekah complains to Isaac of Esau's marriage and connection with the Canaanites.

cell.p:
Quan he iuſted & beð ſo mat,
Toc of kin ðe canaan bi-gat,
For-ði he maked him ſtið & ſtrong,

row.cell: [Fol. 31b.]
Yſaac bad iacob him garen,
Isaac blesses Jacob,
and sends him to Padan-aram.

cell.p: Long weie he gan to-ward aram,
bi cananeam forð he nam,

row.cell: Jacob went a long way about,

And wulde nogt ðat folc bi-twen
Herberged in here huſes ben.
in order to avoid the houses of the Canaanites.

cell.p: He lay bi luzan ut on nigt,
A ſton under hiſe heued rigt,

row.cell: At Luz he tarried all night.

And ſlep and ſag, an ſoðe drem,
fro ðe erðe up til heuene bem,
A leddre ſtonden, and ðor-on
In a dream he saw a ladder reaching from earth to heaven,

cell.p:
Angeles dun-cumen and up-gon,
And ðe louerd ðor uppe a-buuen
Lened[174] ðor-on; and [Jacob] wurð ut-ſuuen,

row.cell: angels ascending and descending, and the Lord stood above it.

cell.p: Herde ðat he quad, "god ic am
ðe luued yſaac and abraham;

row.cell: "I am," He said, "the God of Abraham and of Isaac;

And ðis lond ic ſal giuen ðin ſed,
And in ðis weige don ðe red;
this land will I give thee, and in thy seed shall all mankind be blessed."

cell.p: And i ſal bringen ðe a-gen,
And of ðin kinde bliſced ðu ſalt ben."

div.head: FROM LUZ HE JOURNEYS TO HARAN.

cell.p:
Iacob abraid, & ſeide frigtilike:—
"God in ðis ſtede iſ wittirlike,
Her, dredful ſtede, her, godeſ hus,
Her, heuenegate amonguſ[175] us;

row.cell: Jacob awoke. "Surely," he said, "here is God's house.

cell.p:
Louerd, if ic mote a-gen cumen,
Of ðis ſtede ic ſal in herte munen;"
(Sette he up ðat ſton for muniging,
And get on olige for tok-ning)

row.cell: If I may come again to my father's house,

"He ſal euere min louerd ben,
ðat dede me her ðis ſigt[e] ſen,
the lord shall be my God,

cell.p: Her ic ſal offrendes here don

row.cell: here I shall brake offerings, and yield tithes."

cell.p: Iacob calde ðat ſtede betel;

Quor-fore he it dede, he wiſte wel.
Longe weie he ſiðen ouer-cam,

row.cell: Jacob called the place Bethel.

And longe time or he ſag tharam.
Quane he cam ner, fond he ðor-on
Jacob pursues his journey.

cell.p:
A welle wel helid under a ſton,
And ðre flockes of ſep dor-bi,[176]

row.cell: He finds a well at Haran; three flocks of sheep were lying by it.

cell.p:
ðat ðor abiden al for-ði;
ðor waſ nogt wune on & on,
ðat orf ðor to water gon,

row.cell: The cattle did not go to water one by one, but were all collected together at one time.

Oc at ſet time he ſulden ſamen,
ðor hem-ſelf & here orf framen.
[Fol. 32b.]

cell.p: Iacob ðes hirdes freinen gan,

Hu fer iſt heðen to laban;
Wel he ſeiden and ſwiðe wel,

row.cell: Jacob asks the herdsmen the way to Laban's house.

cell.p:
"loc! her hiſ dogter rachel."
Sep he driuen ðiſ welle ner,
for ghe hem wulde wattre ðer.

row.cell: They answered, "Here is Rachel his daughter." She came to bring the sheep to the well.

Iacob wið hire wente ðat ſton,
And let hire ſep to water gon;
Jacob rolled the stone from the well's mouth.

cell.p: And kidde he was hire mouies ſune,
And kiſte hire aftre kindes wune;

row.cell: He made known his relationship to Rachel.

div.head: JACOB COVENANTS FOR RACHEL.

row.cell:
Rachel was bliðe and forð ghe nam,
And kiddit to hire fader laban.

cell.p: Laban fagnede him in frendes wune,

feren ſwunken yſaaces ſunen.
Iacob tolde him for quat he ſwanc
So fer, and laban herte ranc;
He cuðe him ðer-of wel gret ðhanc,

row.cell: Laban welcomes his nephew and brings him to his house.

cell.p:
And dede him eten and to him dranc,
And ſeide to him, "bi min blod,
ðin come iſ me leflike and good."

row.cell: He entertains him well.

cell.p: Laban bi-tagte him, ſiðen to ſen,
Hiſ hirdeneſſe ðat it wel ben.

row.cell: Jacob abode with Laban for one month,

And quanne a moneð was ouer-meten,
"Iacob," wað he, "quat wiltu bi-geten?
after which time Laban said to him,

cell.p: Quat-ſo [177][ðu] wilt for hire crauen,
Aſke it wið ſkil and ðu ſalt hauen."

row.cell:
[Fol. 33.]
"Tell me what shall thy wages be."

cell.p:
Quat iacob, "ic ſal, for rachel,
Seruen ðe ſeuene winter wel."
Luue wel michil it agte a wold,
Swilc ſeruiſe and ſo longe told.

row.cell: Jacob covenanted for Rachel.

forð geden ſeuene ger bi tale,
And laban made him hiſ bridale;
Seven years passed away and Laban made a feast.

cell.p: Iacob wurð drunken, and euen cam,

Laban bi nigt tog him liam;
And a maiden waſ hire bi-tagt,
Zelfa bi name, ðat ilke nagt.
Iacob gan hire under-fon,

row.cell: When even came Jacob was deceived with Leah.

cell.p:
O morgen ðugte it him miſ-don.
Quat laban, "long wune iſ her driuen,
firmeſt on elde, firſt ben giuen:
And loð me waſ ſenden rachel
So fer, for ic luuede her wel;

row.cell: Laban says that it was not the custom to marry the younger before the first-born.

Oc ſerf me ſeuene oðer ger,
If ðu ſalt rachel ſeruen her;
Jacob agrees to serve other seven years for Rachel.

div.p: At bottom of Fol. 32b is the catchword—"quat ſo ðu wilt."

div.head: JACOB MARRIES RACHEL.

cell.p: Seue nigt ſiðen forð ben numen

Or rachel beð to iacob cumen,
And laban made a feſte oc

Quanne iacob wid[178] rachel toc;
And for ghe ðanne cam him ner,
ſeruede he him ſiðen ſeuene ger.

row.cell: Jacob marries Rachel.

Rachel adde, after londes kire,[179]
maiden balaam to ſeruen hire.
[Fol. 33b.]

cell.p: LIa moder of fowre was,
Ruben, ſymeon, leui, iudas;

row.cell: Leah was the mother of four sons.

for rachel non birðe ne nam,
Sge[180] bi-tagte iacob balaam;
Rachel was barren.

cell.p: bala two childre bar bi him,
Rachel cald es[181] dan(.) neptalim;

row.cell: Bilhah, her handmaid, bare Dan and Naphtali.

And zelfa two ſunes him ber,
Lia calde iſ(.) Gad(.) and aſſer;
Zilpah bare Gad and Asher.

cell.p: Lia ſiðen two ſunes bar,

row.cell: Leah afterwards bare Zebulun, Issachar, and Dinah.

cell.p: Last of rachel iosep was boren,

row.cell: At last Joseph was born of Rachel.

cell.p: Leue aſkede hem hom to faren,
Wið wiues and childre ðeðen charen,

row.cell: Jacob desires leave of Laban to depart.

cell.p: ðat he bi-leue and ſerue him her;

row.cell: Laban would not let him depart.

Wel he ſeið him ðat he ſal hauen
for hire, quat-ſo he wile crauen.
He promises him to give him for hire whatever he shall ask.

cell.p: forward iſ mad of alle ſep,
Of oneſ bles[183] iacob nim kep,

row.cell: And if of ðo ſpotted cumen,
Jacob is to have all the speckled

div.p: Glossed wune in a later hand.

cell.p:
ðo ſulen him ben for hire numen;
Sep or got, haſwed, arled, or grei,
Ben don fro iacob fer a-wei;

row.cell: and spotted cattle for his hire.

ðog him boren ðes oneſ bles
Vn-like manige and likeles.
The flocks produced many speckled and spotted.

cell.p: ðo ſag laban ðat iacob bi-gat
Michil, and him miſlikede ðat;

row.cell: Laban was greatly displeased.

bi-tagte him ðo ðe ſunder bles,
And it him boren ones bles.
He changed Jacob's hire.

cell.p: Ten ſiðes ðus binnen .vi. ger,

Shiftede iacob hirdeneſſe her,
And ai was labaneſ herte ſor,
for hiſ agte wex mor & mor.

row.cell: Ten times within six years he shifted the cattle.

cell.p: Ðo ſag iacob laban wurð wroð,
Vnder him ben leng iſ him loð,

row.cell: Jacob saw that Laban was unfriendly towards him,

And wið iſ wiues he takeð red,
And greiðet him deðenward[184] wið ſped.
so he determined to leave Padanaram.

cell.p: Laban ferde to nimen kep,

In clipping time to hiſe ſep,
fro caram in-to vten ſtede,
ðor quiles iacob ðiſ dede dede;
Wið wiues, and childre, & orf he nam,

row.cell: Laban had left Haran to shear his sheep.

cell.p: And to ðe munt galaad he bi-cam;

row.cell: Jacob came to mount Gilead,
ðanne fleg he to meſopotaniam,
[Fol. 34b.]

And drog to-ward cananeam.
And Rachel adde hid and for-olen
and drew towards Canaan.

cell.p:
Hire faderes godes of gold, & ſtolen.
Laban it wiſte on ðe ðridde dai

row.cell: Rachel had stolen her father's gods.

cell.p:
ðat iacob waſ ðus flogen a-wei;
He toc, and wente, and folwede on,
And ðhogt in mod iacob to ſlon,

row.cell: Laban, hearing of Jacob's flight, pursues him.

Oc god in ſweuene ſpac him to,
ðat he ſulde iacob non yuel do.
God, in a dream, forbids Laban to harm Jacob.

cell.p: vij. nigt forð-geden and dais oc,
Or laban iacob ouer-toc;

row.cell: Laban overtakes Jacob on the seventh day.

div.head: THE COVENANT BETWEEN JACOB AND LABAN.

row.cell:
So waſ he frig[t]ed ear in drem,
ðus meðelike ſpac ðiſ em:

cell.p: "Qui wore ðu fro me for-holen,

And qui aſ ðu min godes ſtolen?
Min mog, min neue, and felage,
Me ne agtes ðu don ſwilc [vn-]lage."
"[I]c was for-dred ðe migte timen,
fro me ðine doutres bi-nimen,

row.cell: He complains of the wrong done to him.

cell.p: wið quam ðu iſ findes, ðat he be dead."

row.cell: Jacob denies that he has been guilty of theft.

Of al ðat laban haued[185] iſ ſogt,
So woren it hid, ne fond he is nogt.
Laban searched for his idols, but found them not.

cell.p: Ðo [q]wað iacob, "yuel iſt bi-togen,

row.cell:
[Fol. 35.]
Then said Jacob, "What is my sin that thou ransackest me as a thief?"

cell.p: ðo quat laban, "frend ſule wit ben,

And trewðe pligt[186] nu unc bi-twen,
And make we it her an hil of ſton,
Name of witneſſe be ðer-on;"
ðor-on he eten bliðe and glað,[187]

row.cell: Quoth Laban, "Friends will we be and plight troth between us."

cell.p:
ðat hil iſ hoten galaað;
Laban hem bliſcede, & on nigt

row.cell: This covenant was made at Gilead.

cell.p:
wente a-gen-ward, or it waſ ligt;
And iacob waſ of weie rad,
Raðe he was fer fro laban ſad.

row.cell: Laban departed before daylight.

cell.p:
Alſ he cam ner cananeam,
Engel wirð a-gen him cam,
Als it were wopnede here,
Redi to ſilden him fro were;

row.cell: As Jacob drew near to Canaan, he was met by the angels of God.

ðat ſtede he calde manaim,
ðor ðis wird of engeles metten him.
ðor he bi-lef, and ſente ðeden[188]
That place he called Mahanaim.

cell.p: Sondere men to freinen and queðen

row.cell: Jacob sends messengers to Esau.

div.head: THE MEETING OF ESAU AND JACOB.

row.cell: If eſau wulde him ogt deren,

cell.p:
ðog wiſte wel god ſulde him weren;
ðor him cam bode him for to ſen,
ðat eſau him cam a-gen;

row.cell: Word came to him that Esau was on his way to meet him.

cell.p:
And iacob ſente fer bi-foren
him riche loac, and ſundri boren,
And iordan he dede ouer waden,

row.cell:
[Fol. 35b.]
Jacob sends a rich present to Esau.

cell.p: And ðor wreſtelede an engel wið,
Senwe ſprungen fro ðe lið;

row.cell: He wrestled with an angel,

(wulde he non ſenwe ſiðen eten,
Self his kinde nile ðat wune forgeten.)
and the sinew shrank from the thigh.

cell.p: Get held he wið ðis angel faſt,

row.cell: Jacob would not let the angel go,

cell.p: Quad iacob, "ðe ne leate ic nogt,
Til ðin bliſcing on me beð wrogt."

row.cell: until he had blessed him.

cell.p:
Ðo quad ðe angel, "ſal tu nummor
ben cald iacob, ſo ðu wore or,
Oc ðu ſal ben hoten iſrael,

for ðu ðe weries ſwiðe wel;
Quan ðe ðe migt wið angel weren,
Hu ſal ani man ðe mugen deren?
Ear iacob and nu iſrael."

row.cell: Jacob prevailed, and his name was called Israel.
This place was called Penuel.

cell.p: Quor eſau a-gen him cam,

row.cell:
[Fol. 36.]
The meeting of Jacob and Esau.

cell.p: And eſau ðo ran him to,
And kiſſede, and wept, ðo rew him ſo.

row.cell: The brothers become reconciled to each other.

div.head: JACOB DWELLS AT SUCCOTH. DINAH'S FOLLY.

cell.p:
ðat ðu to me bringeſt and haueſt ſent."
Iacob was wo ðat he iſ for-ſoc,

row.cell: Esau welcomes Jacob,

And ſcroð him ſo(.) ðat ſum he ðor tok.
Here luue ðo wurð hol and ſchir,
accepts his present,
and departs unto Seir.

cell.p: Iacob fro ðeðen wente, ic wot,

tgelt on a ſtede, and cald it[190] ſochot;
fro ſochot ſiðen to ſichem,

row.cell: From thence Jacob went to Succoth,
And wune ðor-inne ſalem,
and afterwards to Shalem,

cell.p: ðor him ſolde an lond kinge emor,

row.cell: where he bought a piece of land from Hamor.

cell.p: Hiſ dowter dina ðor miſ-dede,
ghe nam leueles fro ðat ſtede,

row.cell: Here his daughter Dinah "mis-did."

[Fol. 36b.]
She went out to see the world.
Shechem took her maidenhead.

cell.p: Symeon and leui it bi-ſpeken,

row.cell: Simeon and Levi slew the Shechemites and spoiled the city.

cell.p:
Til ðat wreche to bale was wrogt,
Oc michil he frigtede for-ði,
boðen ſymeon and leui.

row.cell: Jacob reproved Simeon and Levi for their cruelty.

cell.p: Henden ſichem ne durſten he wunen,
ðat folkes kin god bad him ſunen,

row.cell: They durst not dwell longer at Shechem, but went to Bethel.

And ðeden[191] faren to betel,
And he folgede iſ red on ſel;

cell.p: Agte unclene ne wulde he beren,

row.cell: Their unclean goods they bore not with them.

cell.p: And oðre ydeles brogt fro ſichem,

Gol prenes and ringeſ wið hem,
Diep he iſ dalf under an ooc,
Made him non giſcing in herte wooc.

row.cell: Their idols and gold rings they buried under an oak.

cell.p: Longe it weren ðor for-hid;

Men ſeið for-ði waſ ſo bi-tid,
for ſalamon findin iſ ſal,
And hiſ temple ſriðen wið-al.
Iacob wente fro ðeden[192] in ſped,

row.cell:
[Fol. 37.]
Long they remained buried, until Solomon found them and decked his temple with them.
God sent a fear upon the folk round about, so they did no hurt to the sons of Jacob.

cell.p: He made an alter at betel,
Alſ he god bi-het, ðor he geld wel.

row.cell: Jacob makes an altar at Bethel.
Siðen ðo beniamin was boren,
Benjamin is born.

cell.p:
Rachel adde ðe life for-loren;
Iacob dalf hire and merke dede,
ðat iſ get ſene on ðat ſtede.

row.cell: Rachel dies.

Ðor quiles he wunede at tur ader,
Ruben miſdede wid[194] bala ðer.
At Edar Reuben "misdid" and lay with his father's concubine.

cell.p: Siðen cam iacob to ebron,

And fond his moder of werlde gon;
Starf yſaac quan he waſ hold

row.cell: Jacob arrives at Hebron, and finds his mother gone from this world.

cell.p:
.ix. ſcore ger and fiue told,
And was doluen on ðat ſtede,

row.cell: Isaac dies at the age of nine score years.

cell.p: Oc eſau, ſeyr [and] edon
Lond ydumeam wunede on;

row.cell: Esau dwells in Edom,

div.head: JOSEPH IS HATED BY HIS BRETHREN.

row.cell: Of edon ſo it higte ða,
[Fol. 37b.]

cell.p:
for it was hoten ear bozra.
Hear haued[195] moyſes ouer-gon,

ðor-fore he wended eft a-gon.
xii. ger or yſaac waſ dead

row.cell: which was before called Bozra.
Iacobes ſunes deden un-red;
Jacob's sons did wickedly.

cell.p: FOr ſextene ger ioſeph was old,

Quane he was in-to egipte ſold;
He was iacobes gunkeſte ſune,

row.cell: Joseph was sixteen when sold into Egypt.

cell.p:
Bricteſt of waſpene,[196] and of witter wune,
If he ſag hiſe breðere miſ-faren,

row.cell: Joseph informed his father of his brethren's misdeeds.

cell.p: for-ði wexem[197] wið gret nið

And hate, for it in ille [herte] lið.
ðo wex her hertes niðful & bold
Quanne he hem adde iſ dremeſ told,
ðat hiſ handful ſtod rigt up ſoren,

row.cell: His brethren envied him on account of his dreams.

cell.p: ðat ðu ſalt ðuſ wurðed ben,

row.cell: The vision of the sun, moon, and eleven stars.

ðat ðine breðere, and ic, and ſhe
ðat ðe bar, ſulen luten ðe?"
Jacob reproached his son, yet he believed it should be so.

cell.p: ðuſ he chidden hem bi-twen,
ðoge ðhogte iacob ſiðe it ſulde ben.

row.cell:
Hiſe breðere kepten at ſichem
Hirdneſſe, & iacob to ſen hem
The sons of Jacob kept flocks at Shechem.

cell.p: ſente ioſeph to dalen ebron;

And he was redi his wil to don.
In ſichem feld ne fonde hem nogt,

row.cell: Joseph was sent to see how they fared.

In dotayin he fond hem ſogt;
He knewen him fro feren kumen,
His brethren knew him from afar,

div.head: JOSEPH IS SOLD TO CHAPMEN,

cell.p:
Hate hem on ros, in herte numen;
Swilc nið & hate roſ hem on,

row.cell:
He redden alle him for to ſlon.
"Nai," quad ruben, "ſlo we him nogt,
and took counsel to slay him.

cell.p:
Oðer ſinne may ben wrogt,
Quat-ſo him drempte ðor quiles he ſlep,
In ðiſ ðiſterneſſe,[199] old and dep,
Get wurðe[200] worpen naked and cold,

Quat-ſo hiſ dremeſ owen a-wold."
ðiſ dede waſ don wid[201] herte ſor,

row.cell: Reuben advised them to throw Joseph into an old and deep pit.

cell.p:
Ne wulde ruben nogt drechen ðor;
He gede and ſogte an oðer ſtede,
Hiſ erue in bettre lewſe he dede;

row.cell: Reuben left his brethren to seek better pasture for his cattle.

cell.p: Sag he ðor kumen wid ſpices ware;

row.cell: Judah gave them bad advice,

To-warde egipte he gunne ten.
Iudas tagte hu it ſulde ben,
[Fol. 38b.]

cell.p: Ioseph ſolde ðe breðere ten,

row.cell: and Joseph was sold for thirty pieces of silver.

cell.p: Ðan ruben cam ðider a-gen,

to ðat ciſterneſſe[204] he ran to ſen;
He miſſed Ioseph and ðhogte ſwem,

row.cell: Reuben came thither again and found Joseph gone.

cell.p:
wende him ſlagen, ſet up an rem;
Nile he blinnen, ſwilc ſorwe he cliued,

row.cell: Great was his outcry, which did not cease until he was assured that Joseph lived.

cell.p: In kides blod he wenten it,

ðo waſ ðor-on an rewli lit.
Sondere men he it leiden on,

row.cell: Joseph's coat was dipt in kid's blood,

div.p: he is inserted in the later hand.

div.head: WHO SELL HIM TO POTIPHAR, AN EGYPTIAN.

cell.p:
And ſenten it iacob in-to ebron,
And ſhewed it him, and boden him ſen

row.cell: and sent to Jacob at Hebron.

cell.p: He gret, and ſeide ðat "wilde der
Hauen min ſune ſwolgen her."

row.cell: "Evil beasts," said Jacob, "have swallowed my son."

Hiſ cloðes rent, in haigre ſrid,
Long grot and ſorge is him bi-tid.
Long was his lamentation and sorrow.

cell.p: His ſunes comen him to ſen,
And hertedin him if it migte ben;
And groten ðor min ſunes bale."

row.cell: Jacob would not be comforted for the loss of Joseph.
In hell was a separate abode where the righteous rested,

cell.p:
Til ihesu crist fro ðeden[207] he nam.)
ðe chapmen ſkiuden here fare,

row.cell: till Christ took them from thence.

cell.p:
In-to egipte ledden ðat ware;
wið putifar ðe kinges ſtiward,

He maden ſwiðe bigetel forward,
So michel fe ðor iſ hem told,
He hauen him bogt, he hauen ſold.

row.cell: The merchants took their ware to Egypt.

cell.p: Putifar waſ wol riche man,
And he bogte ioſeph al forðan

row.cell: Potiphar bought Joseph.

cell.p:
He wulde don iſ lechur-hed
wið ioseph, for hiſe faire-hed,
Oc he wurð ðo ſo kinde cold,
To don ſwilc dede adde he no wold;

row.cell: He entertained impure desires towards him,

cell.p:
ſwilc ſelðe cam him fro a-buuen,
God dede it al for ioſeph luue[n].
Biſſop in eliopoli[208]
Men ſeið he was ſiðen for-ði,

row.cell: but Joseph was strengthened from above.

div.p: In [H]Eliopolis; the words are run together.

cell.p:
ðog had he ðo wif(.) and bi-foren
Childre of him bi-geten and of hire boren,
Oc after ðis it ſo bi-cam,
Ioseph iſ dowter to wiue nam.

row.cell: [Fol. 39b.]

Putifar luuede ioſeph wel,
bi-tagte him hiſ huſ euerilc del,
And he wurðede riche man an heg,
Potiphar loved Joseph well.

cell.p:
vnder ioſeph hiſ welðe ðeg.
Hiſ wif wurð wilde, and nam in ðogt

row.cell: His wealth prospered under Joseph's care.

cell.p:
vn-rigt-wiſ luue, and ſwanc for nogt,
One and ſtille ðogt hire gamen
wið ioſeph ſpeken and plaigen ſamen;

row.cell: His wife sought to lead Joseph astray.
For gold nor for wealth of any kind would he "forget his chastity."

cell.p: Often ghe ðrette, often ghe ſcroð,

row.cell: Neither threats nor intreaties prevailed.

cell.p: for he wið hire ne wulde ſpeken,

row.cell: Wherefore she sought to be revenged upon Joseph.

cell.p: And ſeið ioſeph hire wulde don,

ðat ghe ne migte him bringen on;
"ðiſ mentel ic wið-held for-ði,
To tawnen [ðe] ðe ſoðe her-bi."
ðe wite iſ hiſe(.) ðe right iſ hire,
God al-migtin ðe ſoðe ſhire.

row.cell:
[Fol. 40.]
She accused him falsely to Potiphar,
who, believing his wife's tale,

cell.p: And holden harde in priſun.

row.cell: threw Joseph into prison.
An litel ſtund, quile he waſ ðer,

So gan him luuen ðe priſuner,
And him de[211] chartre haueð bi-tagt,
The gaoler loved Joseph.

cell.p:
wið ðo priſunes to liuen in hagt.
Or for miſdede, or for on-ſagen,
ðor woren to ðat priſun dragen,

row.cell: In this prison, either for misdeed or bad words,

cell.p: On ðat ðe kingeſ kuppe bed,
And on ðe made ðe kingeſ bred;

row.cell: were placed the chief butler and baker.

cell.p: At here drink and at here mel,

row.cell: Both dreamt dreams in one night,

He herde hem murnen(.) he hem freinde for-quat;
Harde dremes ogen awold ðat.
which caused them to become very sorrowful.

cell.p: ðo ſeide he to ðe butuler,
"Tel me ðin drem, mi broðer her.

row.cell: Joseph inquired the reason of their grief.

Queðer-ſo it wurðe ſofte or ſtrong,
ðe reching wurð on god bi-long."
[Fol. 40b.]
"Me drempte, ic ſtod at a win-tre,
The butler's dream.

cell.p:
ðat adde waxen buges ðre,
Oreſt it blomede, and ſiðen bar

row.cell: A vine with three branches

ðe beries ripe wurð ic war;
ðe kinges [kuppe] ic hadde on hond,
bore grapes;

cell.p:
ðe beries ðor-inne me ðhugte ic wrong,
And bar it drinken to pharaon,
Me drempte, alſ ic waſ wune to don."

row.cell: the juice the butler squeezed into Pharaoh's cup, and gave him to drink as he was wont.

cell.p: "Good is," quað Ioſeph, "to dremen of win,
heilneſſe an bliſſe iſ ðer-in;

row.cell: "Good it is," said Joseph, "to dream of wine.
In three days thou shalt be restored to thy office,

cell.p:
Of me ðu ðhenke ðan it ſal ben,
Bed min herdne to pharaon,
ða[t] ic ut of prisun wurðe don,

row.cell: then think of me and bear my errand to Pharaoh,

cell.p: for ic am ſtolen of kinde lond,
and her wrigteleſlike holden in bond."

row.cell: for I am here wrongfully held in prison."

cell.p:
Quað ðis bred-wrigte, "liðeð nu me,
me drempte ic bar bread-lepes ðre,
And ðor-in bread and oðer meten,
Quilke ben wune ðe kinges to eten;

row.cell: The "breadwright's" dream.

And fugeles hauen ðor-on lagt,
ðor-fore ic am in ſorge and hagt,
Fowls seized on the baskets of bread intended for the king,
for ic ne migte me nogt weren,
and he could not keep the meat from them.

cell.p: ðu ſalt, after ðe ðridde dei,

ben do on rode, weila-wei!
And fugeles ſulen ði fleis to-teren,
ðat ſal non agte mugen ðe weren."
Soð wurð ſo ioſeph ſeide ðat,

row.cell: "In three days," said Joseph, "thou shalt be hanged, and fowls shall tear thy flesh in pieces."

cell.p: ðis buteler Ioſeph ſone for-gat.

row.cell: The butler soon forgat Joseph.

Two ger ſiðen was Ioſeph ſperd
ðor in priſun wið-uten erd;
After two years,
Ðo drempte pharaon king a drem,
Pharaoh dreamt a dream.

cell.p:
ðat he ſtod bi ðe flodes ſtrem,
And ðeden[212] ut-comen .vii. neet,
Euerilc wel ſwiðe fet and gret,
And .vii. lene after ðo,
ðe deden ðe .vii. fette wo,

row.cell: He stood by the river, and there came seven "neat" fat and great, and seven lean after,
which ate up the fat ones.

cell.p:
.vii. eares wexen fette of coren,
On an busk ranc and wel tidi,
And .vii. lene rigt ðor-bi,
welkede, and ſmale, and drugte numen,
ðe ranc he hauen ðo ouer-cumen,

row.cell: Seven full ears of corn sprang up "on a rank bush," and then came seven withered ears,

cell.p:
To-ſamen it ſmiten and, on a ſtund,
ðe fette ðriſt hem to ðo grund.
ðe king abraid and woc in ðhogt,
ðeſ dremes ſwep ne wot he nogt,

row.cell:
[Fol. 41b.]
which smote the others to the ground.

Ne was non ſo wis man in al hiſ lond,
ðe kude vn-don ðis dremes bond;
None were found able to interpret the dreams.

cell.p: ðo him bi-ðhogte ðat buteler

Of ðat him drempte in priſun ðer,
And of ioſeph in ðe priſun,
And he it tolde ðe king pharaun.

row.cell: The butler bethought him of Joseph.

cell.p: Ioſeph waſ ſone in priſun ðo hogt,
And ſhauen, & clad, & to him brogt;

row.cell: Joseph is taken from prison,

ðe king him bad ben hardi & bold,
If he can rechen ðis dremeſ wold;
and brought before Pharaoh,

cell.p: He told him quat him drempte o nigt,
And ioſep rechede his drem wel rigt.

row.cell: who related to him his dreams.
"The two dreams," answered Joseph, "are one."

cell.p:
In al fulſum-hed ſulen it ben numen,
And .vij. oðere ſulen after ben,

row.cell: "Seven years of plenty

cell.p:
Sori and nedful men ſulen iſ ſen;
Al ðat ðiſe firſt .vii. maken,
Sulen ðiſ oðere .vii. roſpen & raken;

row.cell: shall be followed by seven years of famine.

Ic rede ðe king, nu her bi-foren,
To maken laðes and gaderen coren,
I advise thee to make barns and store up corn, that thy folk perish not."

cell.p: ðat ðin folc ne wurð vnder-numen,

Quan ðo hungri gere ben forð-cumen."
King pharaon liſtnede hiſe red,
ðat wurð him ſiðen ſeli ſped.
He bi-tagte ioſep hiſ ring,
And his bege of gold for wurðing,

row.cell: Pharaoh gave Joseph his ring,

cell.p:
And bad him al hiſ lond bi-ſen,
And under him hegeſt for to ben,
And bad him welden in hiſ hond
His folc, and agte, & al his lond;

row.cell: and bad him rule the whole land.

cell.p:
ðo waſ vnder him ðanne putifar,
And hiſ wif ðat hem ſo to-bar.
Ioſep to wiue his dowter nam,
Oðer is nu quan ear bi-cam;

row.cell: Then were Potiphar and his wife under him.

div.head: THE FAMINE IN EGYPT AND CANAAN.

cell.p: He luueden god, he geld it hem.

row.cell: Before the famine came two sons were born to Joseph.

cell.p: ðo ynug [was] vnder his hond.

row.cell: The years of plenty pass away.

Hvnger wex in lond chanaan,
And his .x. ſunes iacob for-ðan
The famine was felt in Canaan.

cell.p: Sente in-to egipt to bringen coren;
He bilef at hom ðe was gungeſt boren.

row.cell: Jacob sent his ten sons to Egypt to buy corn.

ðe .x. comen, for nede ſogt,
To Ioſep, and he ne knewen him nogt,
[Fol. 42b.]

cell.p: And ðog he lutten him frigtilike,

Anð ſeiden to him mildelike,
"We ben ſondes for nede driuen
To bigen coren ðor-bi to liuen."

row.cell: Though they honoured Joseph,

cell.p: (Ioſep hem knew al in his ðhogt,

Alſ he let he knew hem nogt.)
"It ſemet wel ðat ge ſpies ben,

row.cell: yet he pretended not to know them.

cell.p:
And in-to ðiſ lond cumen to ſen,
And cume ge for non oðer ðing,

but for to ſpien ur lord ðe king."
"Nai," he ſeiden euerilc on,

row.cell: He accused them of being spies.

cell.p:
"Spies were we neuer non,
Oc alle we ben on faderes ſunen,

row.cell: They declared that they were true men, the sons of one father.

cell.p: Hu ſulde oni man[214] poure for-geten,

ſwilke and ſo manige ſunes bigeten?
for ſeldum bi-tid ſelf ani king
ſwilc men to ſen of hiſe ofſpring."

row.cell: "Only kings," said Joseph, "had so many sons."

cell.p: "A louerd, merci! get iſ ðor on

row.cell: "One," the brethren said, "is at home with his father."

cell.p: "Nu, bi ðe feið ic og to king pharaon,

ſule ge nogt alle eðen gon,
Til ge me bringen beniamin,
ða gungeſte broðer of pore[215] kin."
For ðo waſ Ioſep ſore for-dred

ðat he wore oc ðhurg hem for-red;
He dede hem binden, and leden dun,

row.cell:
[Fol. 43.]
Quoth Joseph, "Ye shall not all go hence, until ye bring me Benjamin."

cell.p:
And ſperen faſte in his priſun;
ðe ðridde dai he let hem gon,

Al but ðe ton broðer ſymeon;
ðiſ ſymeon bi-lef ðor in bond,
To wedde under Ioſepes hond.
ðes oðere breðere, ſone on-on,
Token leue and wenten hom;

row.cell: He kept them in prison, and on the third day let them all go except Simeon.

And ſone he weren ðeden[216] went,
Wel ſore he hauen hem bi-ment,
And ſeiden hem ðan ðor bi-twen,
The others bemoaned their ill-luck.

cell.p:
"Wrigtful we in ſorwe ben,
for we ſinigeden quilum or
On hure broðer michil mor,
for we werneden him merci,

Nu drege we ſorge al for-ði."
Wende here non it on hiſ mod,
Oc Ioſep al it under-ſtod.

row.cell: They thought of their sin towards Joseph.

cell.p: Ioſepes men ðor quiles deden
Al-ſo Ioſep hem adde beden;

row.cell: Joseph's men did, meanwhile, as they were commanded,

cell.p:
ðo breðere ſeckes hauen he filt,
And in euerilc ðe ſiluer pilt
ðat ðor was paid for ðe coren,

row.cell:
[Fol. 43b.]
and filled the brothers' sacks, and placed in them the money paid for the corn.

cell.p: Oc alle he weren ouer-ðogt,

row.cell: Unopened they brought them to Jacob and told him how they had sped.

cell.p: And quan men ðo ſeckes ðor un-bond,

And in ðe coren ðo agtes fond,
Alle he woren ðanne[217] ſori ofrigt.
Iacob ðus him bi-meneð o-rigt,

row.cell: Great was their fear when they saw the money in the sack's mouth.

cell.p: "Wel michel ſorge is me bi-cumen,
ðat min two childre aren me for-numen;

row.cell: "Much sorrow," says Jacob, "is come upon me,

cell.p: Dead and ſorge me ſegeð on;

row.cell: since my two children are taken from me.

cell.p:
Ai ſal beniamin wið me bi-lewen
ðor quiles ic ſal on werlde liuen."
ðo quað iudas, "us ſal ben hard,
If we no[218] holden him non forward."

row.cell: Benjamin shall remain with me."

Wex derke,[219] ðis coren iſ gon,
Iacob eſt[220] bit hem faren agon,
The corn is soon consumed, and Jacob bids them go to Egypt for more.

cell.p: Oc he ne duren ðe weie cumen in,
"but ge wið uſ ſenden beniamin;"

row.cell:
ðo quað he, "quan it iſ ned,
And ne can no bettre red,
Jacob is persuaded to send Benjamin.

cell.p: Bereð dat[221] ſiluer hol agon,
ðat hem ðor-of ne wante non,

row.cell: He sends back the silver,

And oðer ſiluer ðor bi-foren,
for to bigen wið oðer coren;
and other corn-money,

cell.p: fruit and ſpices of dere priſ,

row.cell: together with a present of fruit and spices for Joseph.

cell.p: ðo nomen he forð weie rigt,
Til he ben cumen in-to egypte ligt;

row.cell: The brethren come again to Egypt.

And quanne Ioſep hem alle ſag,
Kinde ðogt in his herte was [ðag].
Joseph treats them kindly,

cell.p: He bad hiſ ſtiward gerken iſ meten,

He ſeide he ſulden wið him alle eten;
He ledde hem alle to Ioſepes biri,
Her non hadden ðo loten miri.
"Louerd," he ſeiden ðo euerilc on,

row.cell: and bids his steward prepare a feast for them.

cell.p:
"Gur ſiluer iſ gu brogt a-gon,
It was in ure ſeckes don,
Ne wiſte ur non gilt ðor-on."
"Beð nu ſtille," quad ſtiward,
"for ic nu haue min forward."

row.cell: They tell Joseph that they have brought back the silver which they found in their sacks.

cell.p: for he was numen ðor to nome.

row.cell:
[Fol. 44b.]
Simeon was brought out unto them.
Joseph came home about noon,

cell.p:
fellen bi-forn ðat louerd-iſ fot,
And bedden him riche preſent
ðat here fader hi[m] adde ſent;
And he leuelike it under-ſtod,
for alle he weren of kinde blod.

row.cell: and the brethren offered him their present.

"LIueð," quad he, "ðat fader get,
ðat ðus manige ſunes bi-gat?"
He inquires after his father.

cell.p: "louerd," he ſeiden, "get he liueð,
Wot ic ðor non ðat he ne biueð;

row.cell: They answer that Jacob is well,

cell.p:
And ðiſ iſ gunge beniamin,
Hider brogt after bode-word ðin."
ðo Iosep ſag him ðor bi-foren,
Bi fader & moder broðer boren,

row.cell: and that Benjamin stands before him.

Him ouer-wente his herte on-on,
Kinde luue gan him ouer-gon;
Joseph was overcome.

cell.p: Sone he gede ut and ſtille he gret,
ðat al his wlite wurð teres wet.

row.cell: He went out and wept secretly.

After ðat grot, he weiſ iſ wliten,
And cam ðan in and bad hem eten
After a while he returned to them and bade them eat.

div.head: THE BRETHREN ARE ACCUSED OF THEFT.

cell.p: He dede hem waſſen and him bi-foren,

row.cell:
[Fol. 45.]
He made his brethren sit before him according to their age.

cell.p: Of euerilc ſonde, of euerilc win,

moſt and beſt he gaf beniamin.
In fulſum-hed he wurðen glaðe,[222]
Ioſep ne ðoht ðor-of no ſcaðe,
Oc it him likede ſwiðe wel,

row.cell: Of meat and wine, the best he gave to Benjamin.
Joseph gave them good counsel,

cell.p: "And al ðe bettre ſule ge ſpeden,
If ge wilen gu wið treweiðe leden."

row.cell: and advised them to act truthfully.

cell.p:
Eft on morwen quan it waſ dai,
Or or ðe breðere ferden a-wei,
Here ſeckes woren alle filt wið coren,
And ðe ſiluer ðor-in bi-foren;

row.cell: On the morrow they depart.

cell.p: Ioſep haueð hem after ſent.

row.cell: Joseph's cup is hid in Benjamin's sack.

ðis ſonde hem ouertakeð raðe,
And bi-calleð of harme and ſcaðe;
Joseph's messenger overtakes them,

cell.p: "Vn-ſeli men, quat haue ge don?
Gret vn-ſelðehe iſ gu cumen on,

row.cell: and accuses them of theft.
[Fol. 45b.]

cell.p:
"Vp quam ðu it findes witterlike,
He ſlagen and we agen driuen
In-to ðraldom, euermor to liuen."

row.cell: The brethren assert their innocence.

cell.p: He gan hem ranſaken on and on,

And fond it ðor ſone a-non,
And nam ðo breðere euerilk on,
And ledde hem ſorful a-gon,

row.cell: They are ransacked one by one,

div.head: JOSEPH MAKES HIMSELF KNOWN TO HIS BRETHREN.

cell.p: And brogte hem bi-for ioſep

Wid reweli lote, and ſorwe, and wep.
ðo quat ioſep, "ne wiſte ge nogt

row.cell: and brought before Joseph,

cell.p:
ðat ic am o wol witter ðogt?
Mai nogt longe me ben for-holen
Quat-ſo-euere on londe wurð ſtolen."

row.cell: who reproaches them for their crime.

cell.p:
ic ledde [him] ut on trewthe min,
ðat he ſulde ef[223] cumen a-gen
to hiſe fader, and wið him ben."

row.cell: Judah tells Joseph of his promise to his father.

cell.p: ðo cam ioſep ſwilc rewðe up-on,

he dede halle ut ðe toðere gon,
And ſpac un-eðes, ſo e gret,
ðat alle hiſe wlite wurð tereſ wet.

row.cell: Joseph commands all, except his brethren, to leave him, and makes himself known to them.

cell.p: "Ic am ioſep, dredeð gu nogt,

for gure helðe or hider brogt;
Two ger ben nu ðat derke[224] iſ cumen,
Get ſulen .v. fulle ben numen,
ðat men ne ſulen ſowen ne ſheren,
So ſal drugte ðe feldes deren.

row.cell:
Rapeð gu to min fader a-gen,
And ſeið him quilke min bliſſes ben,
And doð him to me cumen hider,
Tells them to hasten to his father,

cell.p:
And ge and gure orf al to-gider;
Of lewſe god in lond gerſen
ſulen ge ſundri riche ben."
Euerilc he kiſte, on ilc he gret,
Ilc here was of iſ teres wet.

row.cell: and return with their cattle to Egypt.

cell.p:
ðat Ioſep wulde him ðider dragen,
for luue of Ioſep migte he timen.

row.cell: Soon did Pharaoh learn the new tidings.
He bad cartes and waines nimen,
He bad them take carts and

div.head: JACOB AND HIS FAMILY GO INTO EGYPT.

cell.p: And fechen wiues, and childre, and men,

And gaf hem ðor al lond gerſen,
And het hem ðat he ſulden hauen
More and bet ðan he kude crauen.

row.cell: wains and fetch their wives and children.

cell.p: Ioſep gaf ilc here twinne ſrud,
Beniamin moſt he[225] made prud;

row.cell: Joseph gave them changes of raiment.

fif weden beſt bar beniamin,
ðre hundred plates of ſiluer fin,
Al-ſo fele oðre ðor-til,
[Fol. 46b.]

cell.p:
He bad ben in is faderes wil,
And .x. aſſes wið ſemes feſt;
Of alle egiptes welðhe beſt
Gaf he iſ breðere, wið herte bliðe,

row.cell: He bad them take presents for Jacob,
and hasten homeward.

cell.p: And quane he comen him bi-foren,
Ne wiſte he nogt quat he woren.

row.cell: When they came home, Jacob scarcely recognized them.

cell.p:
"Louerd," he ſeiden, "iſrael,
Ioſep ðin ſune greteð ðe wel,
And ſendeð ðe bode ðat he liueð,
Al egipte in hiſ wil cliueð."
