row.cell: "Lord Israel," they said, "Joseph liveth and greeteth thee well."

cell.p:
Iacob a-braid, and trewed it nogt,
Til he ſag al ðat welðe brogt.
"Wel me," quað he, "wel iſ me wel,
ðat ic aue abiden ðuſ ſwil[c] ſel!

row.cell: Jacob believed not till he saw the presents.

And ic ſal to min ſune fare
And ſen, or ic of werlde chare."
Then he said, "I shall go to my son ere I turn from the world."

cell.p: [I]Acob wente ut of lond chanaan,

row.cell: Jacob and his family left Canaan.
for ðat he weren hirde-men,

cell.p:
He bad hem ben in lond gerſen.
Iacob waſ brogt bi-foren ðe king
for to geuen him hiſ bliſcing.

row.cell: Pharaoh gives them the land of Goshen to live in. Jacob is brought before Pharaoh,

div.head: THEY DWELL IN THE LAND OF GOSHEN.

cell.p: "fader derer," quað pharaon,
"hu fele ger be ðe on?"

row.cell:
"An hundred ger and .xxx. mo
Haue ic her drogen in werlde wo,
ðog ðinkeð me ðor-offen fo,
and tells him of his age,

cell.p:
ðog ic iſ haue drogen in wo,
ſiðen ic gan on werlde ben,
Her vten erd, man-kin bi-twen;
So ðinked[226] euerilc wiſ man,

row.cell: of his many sorrows,

cell.p:
ðe wot quor-of man-kin bi-gan,
And ðe of adames gilte muneð,
ðat he her uten herdes wuneð."

row.cell: and how all suffer for the sin of Adam.

cell.p: Pharaon bad him wurðen wel
ðe waſ y-oten Rameſé.

row.cell: Pharaoh bad him rest in peace.

Iacob on liue wunede ðor
In reſte fulle .xiiij. ger;
Jacob lived one hundred and forty-four years.

cell.p: And god him let bi-foren ſen
Quilc time hiſe ending ſulde ben;

row.cell: God showed him the time of his death.

He bad ioſep hiſe leue ſune,
On ðhing ðat[227] offe wel mune,
ðat quan it wurð mid him don,

[Fol. 47b.]
Jacob bad Joseph promise

cell.p:
He ſulde him birien in ebron;
And witterlike he it aueð him ſeid,

row.cell: to bury him in Hebron,

cell.p:
ðe ſtede ðor abraham was leid;
So was him lif[228] to wurðen leid,
Quuor ali gast ſtille hadde ſeid

row.cell: where Abraham was laid,

cell.p: He ðogt wið hem reſte to hauen.

row.cell: and his elders before him.

Ioſep ſwor him al-ſo he bad,
And he ðor-of wurð bliðe & glad.
Joseph swore to do as his father wished.

cell.p: Or ðan he wiſte off werlde faren,

He bade hiſe kinde to him charen,
And ſeide quat of hem ſulde ben,
Hali gaſt dede it him ſeen;
In clene ending and ali lif,
So he for-let ðis werldes ſtrif.

row.cell: Before he died Jacob called his sons before him, and "said what of them should be."
Joseph caused his father's body to be embalmed.

cell.p:
And egipte folc him bi-waken
xl. nigtes and .xl. daiges,
ſwilc woren egipte lages.

row.cell: Egypt's folk "bewaked" Jacob for forty nights and forty days.

cell.p: first .ix. nigt ðe liches beðen,

row.cell:
[Fol. 48.]
The first nine nights they bathe, anoint, etc., the body.

cell.p: And ebriſſe folc adden an kire,
Nogt ſone deluen it wið yre,

row.cell: The Hebrews had a different custom;
Oc waſſen it and kepen it rigt,
they wash the body,

cell.p:
Wið-vten ſmerles, ſeuene nigt,
And ſiden[229] ſmered .xxx. daiges.

Criſtene folc haueð oðer laiges,
He ben ſmered ðor quiles he liuen,

row.cell: and keep it unanointed for seven nights.

cell.p:
Wið criſme and olie, in trewðe geuen;
for trewðe and gode dedes mide,
ðor quiles ðat he wunen her,

row.cell: Christian folks are anointed with chrism and oil in their life-time.

cell.p: Wel him mai ben dat[231] wel it dede!

row.cell: For the dead they perform alms-gift and mass-song.

Egipte folc aueð him waked
xl. nigt, and feſte maked,
Jacob's sons kept a "wake" of thirty days.

div.head: HE IS BURIED IN HEBRON.

cell.p: And hiſe ſunes .xxx. daiges,
In clene lif and ali daiges;[232]

row.cell:
So woren forð .x. wukes gon,
get adde Iacob birigeles non.
And pharaon king cam bode bi-foren,

[Fol. 48b.]
So ten weeks passed away and Jacob had no burial.

cell.p:
ðat Ioſep haueð his fader ſworen;
And he it him gatte ðor he wel dede,

row.cell: Pharaoh heard of Joseph's oath to his father,

cell.p:
And bad him nimen him feres mide,
Wel wopnede men and wiſ of here[n],

And bi-mening for iacob deden;
So longe he hauen ðeðen numen,

row.cell: and gave him leave to bury his father, and to take with him "weaponed" men.

cell.p:
To flum iurdon ðat he ben cumen,
And ouer pharan til ebron;

ðor iſ ðat liche in biriele don,
And Ioſep in-to egipte went,
Wid[234] al iſ folc ut wið him ſent.

row.cell: They crossed the Jordan, and laid the body in a tomb, and Joseph returned to Egypt.

cell.p: Hiſe breðere comen him ðanne to,

And gunnen him bi-ſeken alle ſo;
"Vre fader," he ſeiden, "or he was dead,
Vs he ðiſ bodewurd ſeigen bead,
Hure ſinne ðu him for-giue,
Wið-ðanne-ðat we vnder ðe liuen."

row.cell: His brethren came to him to seek forgiveness,

Alle he fellen him ðor to fot,
To beðen meðe and bedden oc;
and fell down there before his feet, and he forgave and loved them kindly.

cell.p: And he it for-gaf[235] hem mildelike,
And luuede hem alle kinde-like.

row.cell:
[I]Oſep an hundred ger waſ hold,
And hiſ kin wexen manige-fold;
Joseph waxed old;

cell.p: He bad ſibbe cumen him bi-foren,
Or he waſ ut of werlde boren;

row.cell: he bad his relations come before him ere he died,

div.p: At the bottom of fol. 48b is the catchword—"And he it for-gaff."

row.cell: "It ſal," quað he, "ben ſoð, bi-foren

cell.p:
ðat god hað ure eldere ſworen;
He ſal gu leden in hiſ hond

row.cell: and told them of God's promise to their elders.

cell.p: ðat mine bene ne be for-loren,

wið gu ben mine bones boren."
He it him gatten and wurð he dead,
God do ðe ſoule ſeli red!

row.cell: He asks them to bear his bones with them, when they leave Egypt.

cell.p: Hiſe liche waſ ſpice-like maked,

And longe egipte-like waked,
And ðo biried hem bi-foren,
And ſiðen late of londe boren.
Hiſe oðre breðere, on and on,
Woren ybiried at ebron.

row.cell: The death of Joseph.

cell.p:
An her endede to ful, in wiſ,
ðe boc ðe iſ hoten geneſis,
ðe moyſes, ðurg godes red,
Wrot for lefful ſoules ned.

row.cell: Here endeth the book called Genesis, written by Moses, through God's counsel.

God ſchilde hiſe ſowle fro helle bale,
ðe made it ðus on engel tale!
And he ðat ðiſe lettres wrot,

[Fol. 49b.]
God shield his soul from hell-bale, who translated it into English!

cell.p:
God him helpe weli mot,
And berge iſ ſowle fro ſorge & grot
Of helle pine, cold & hot!
And alle men, ðe it heren wilen,[236]

row.cell: May God help and protect him from hell-pain, cold and hot!

cell.p:
God leue hem in hiſ bliſſe ſpilen
Among engeles & ſeli men,
Wiðuten ende in reſte ben,
And luue & pais uſ bi-twen,
And god ſo graunte, amen, ameN!

row.cell: And all men who will hear it, God grant that they may dwell in bliss among angels for ever!
GOdes bliſcing be wið vs,
Her nu bi-ginned[237] exodus.
Here beginneth Exodus.

cell.p: Pharao kinges rigte name

Vephres, be dede ðe ebriſ frame;
And bi oðere ſeuene kinges ſel,

row.cell: Under Pharaoh, and the seven kings who succeeded him,
Wexen he ðore & ðogen wel.
the Israelites increased and prospered.

cell.p: ðe egtenede king amonaphis,
Agenes ðis folc hatel is;

row.cell: The eighth king treated them harshly,

cell.p:
And egipte folc adden nið,
for ebriſ adden ſeli ſið.
Quuað ðis ging[238] wið hem ſtille in red,
"ðis ebris waxen michil ſped,

row.cell: and the Egyptians became jealous of them.

Bute if we eraflike[239] hem for-don,
Ne ſulen he non eige ſen uſ on."

cell.p: Ðo ſette ſundri hem to waken

row.cell: They made slaves of them, and set them to build walls.

cell.p: Summe he deden in vn-ðewed ſwinc,
for it was fugel and ful o ſtinc,

row.cell: Some they made to do foul work,
to carry "muck and fen out of the city,"

cell.p:
He deden hem crepen dikes long,
And wide a-buten burges gon,

row.cell: and to creep along dikes.

cell.p:
And cumen ðer ear waſ non;
And if ðat folc hem wulde deren,

ðe dikeſ comb hem ſulde weren.
for al ðat ſwinc heui & ſor,

row.cell: The comb of the dike serves them as protection against their enemies.

cell.p:
Ay wex ðat kinde, mor & mor,
And ðhogen, & ſpredden in londe ðor,
ðat made ðe kinges herte ful ſor.

row.cell: For all that labour, the folk increased and spread.

Ðo bad monophis pharaun
wimmen ben ſet in euerilc tun,
Then bad Pharaoh,

cell.p: And ðat he weren redi bi-foren,
Quan ebru child ſuld be boren,

row.cell: that every Hebrew male child should be put to death as soon as it was born.

div.head: THE BIRTH AND PRESERVATION OF MOSES.

row.cell:
And ðe knapes to deade giuen,
And leten ðe mayden childre liuen.

cell.p: Oc he it leten fro godeſ dred;

Get ðo childre wexen in ſped,
And quane he komen to ðe king,

row.cell:
[Fol. 50b.]
The midwives saved the children's lives,

He wereden hem wið leſing;
He ſeiden ðe childre weren boren
and lied to the king, saying,

cell.p:
Or he migten ben hem bi-foren.
God it geald ðeſe wifes wel,
On hom, on hagte, eddi ſel!

row.cell: that the children were born ere they arrived.

cell.p: Ðo bad ðis king al opelike,

In alle burges modilike,
Euerilc knape child of ðat kin
ben a-non don ðe flod wið-in.

row.cell: Pharaoh then bad that every "knave child" should be drowned.

cell.p: BI ðat time waſ moyſes boren,

row.cell: By that time was Moses born.

cell.p: wel is hire of bird[241] bi-tid.

row.cell: His mother hid him for three months.

cell.p: In an fetles, of rigeſſes wrogt,
Terred, ðat water dered it nogt,

row.cell: Then she made an ark,
ðiſ child wunden ghe wulde don,
placed the child in it,
And ſetten it ſo ðe water on;
and set it on the water.
Ghe adde or hire dowter ſent,
Miriam was sent to watch what became of it.

cell.p: Teremuth kinkes[242] dowter ðor cam,

row.cell: The king's daughter came and saw the child on the water.

cell.p: Ghe wiſte it was of ebrius kin,
And ðog cam hire rewde[243] wið-in;

row.cell: She wist it was of Hebrew kin,

div.head: TEREMUTH ADOPTS HIM AS HER SON.

row.cell: God haued[244] ſwilc fair-hed him geuen,
ðat ſelf ðe fon it leten liuen.
but let it live for its beauty.

cell.p: Egipte wimmen comen ner,

And boden ðe childe letten ðer,
Oc he wente it awei wið rem,
Of here bode nam he no gem.

row.cell: Egyptians wanted her to destroy the child.

cell.p: ÐO quad maria to teremuth,

"wilt ðu, leuedi, ic go fear out,
And take ſum wimman of ðat kin
ðor he waſ bi-gote & foſtred in?"

row.cell: Miriam, at Teremuth's bidding,

cell.p: Teremuth ſo bad, & ſche forð-ran,

And brogt hire a foſtre wimman,
On waſ tette he ſone aueð lagt,

row.cell: fetches a "foster woman" for the child.

cell.p:
And teremuth haueð hire him bi-tagt.
Iakabeð wente bliðe agen,

row.cell: Teremuth consigned Moses to Jochabed, who returned home blithely.

cell.p: And quane it ſulde ſundred ben,
Ghe wiſte of water it boren ben.

row.cell:
[Fol. 51b.]
When old enough, the child was adopted by Teremuth, who called it Moses.

cell.p:
An time after ðat ðiſ was don,
Ghe brogte him bi-foren pharaon,
And ðiſ king wurð him in herte mild,

row.cell: She brought him before Pharaoh, who placed the royal crown on his head.

cell.p: ðe child it warp dun to de grund.

row.cell: The child soon threw it to the ground.

Hamonel[247] likeneſ was ðor-on;
ðis crune is broken, ðiſ iſ miſdon.
Hamon's likeness was thereon.

cell.p: Biſſop Eliopoleos
ſag ðiſ timing, & up he roſ;

row.cell: The Bishop of Heliopolis saw this, and said,

cell.p:
"If ðiſ child," quad he, "mote ðen,
He ſal egyptes bale ben."
If ðor ne wore helpe twen lopen,
ðiſ witterlike, or in child-hede;"

row.cell: "If this child be allowed to thrive, he shall become Egypt's bale."

cell.p:
He bad ðis child brennen to colen
And he toc is hu migt he it ðolen,
And in hiſe muth ſo depe he iſ dede

row.cell:
[Fol. 52.]
The king offered the child two burning coals (to eat), and he put them in his mouth, and burnt the end of his tongue therewith, and spake indistinctly.

cell.p: Oc ſo faiger he waſ on to ſen,

ðat migte non man modi ben.
ðor quiles he ſeweden him up-on,
Mani dede b[i]leph un-don
In ðat burg folc bi-twen,
So waſ hem lef on him to ſen.

row.cell: So fair was he to look upon, that none might be angry with him.

cell.p:
Bi dat[249] time ðat he was guð,
Wið faigered and ſtrengthe kuð,
folc ethiopienes on egipte cam,

row.cell: By the time that he became renowned for beauty and strength, the Ethiopians invaded Egypt, and burnt and slew as far as the Red Sea.

cell.p: ðo was egipte folc in dred,

row.cell: The Egyptians ask counsel of their gods, who tell them that a Hebrew shall deliver them.

cell.p:
ðat moyſes ſal wið hire forð-nimen,
Or haue he hire pligt & ſworen,
ðat him ſal feið wurðful ben boren.

row.cell: Moses is permitted by Teremuth

cell.p: Moyſes was louered of ðat here,
ðor he wurð ðane egyptes were;

row.cell: [Fol. 52b.]
to lead the Egyptians against their enemies.

cell.p: He bi-loc hem & ſmette a-mong,

row.cell: He smote and slew them.

cell.p:
And ſlug ðor manige; oc ſumme flen,
Into ſaba to borgen ben.
Moyſes bi-ſette al ðat burg,
Oc it was riche & ſtrong ut-ðhurg;

row.cell: Many fled to Sheba.

Ethiopienes kinges dowter tarbis,
Riche maiden of michel priſ,
The king of Ethiopia's daughter, for love,

cell.p: Gaf ðiſ riche burg moyſi;

Luue-bonde hire ghe it dede for-ði.
ðor iſe fon he leide in bonde,

row.cell: gave this rich city to Moses,

And he wurð al-migt-ful in ðat lond;
He bi-lef ðor(.) tarbis him ſcroð,
who waxed mighty in the land.

cell.p:
ðog was him ðat ſurgerun ful loð;
Mai he no leue at hire taken

row.cell: His sojourn there was distasteful to him,

but-if he it mai wið crafte maken:
He waſ of an ſtrong migt wiſ,
but by craft he brought it to an end.

cell.p:
He carf in two gummes of priſ
Two likeneſſes, ſo grauen & meten,

row.cell: He carved upon two gems two likenesses;

ðiſ doð ðenken, & ðoð[251] forgeten;
He feſt is in two ringes of gold,
the one caused remembrance, the other forgetfulness.

cell.p: Gaf hire ðe ton, he was hire hold;

row.cell: Moses gave her the one which caused her to forget her love,

cell.p: Into egypte e[254] wente a-gen.

row.cell: and so he came again to Egypt.
On a time he went to Goshen, and found a "moody steward" beating a Hebrew.

cell.p: And hente ðe cherl wið hiſe wond,
And he fel dun in dedes bond;

row.cell: He seized the churl, slew him, and buried him in the sand.

And moyſes drug him to ðe ſtrond,
And ſtille[256] he dalf him [in] ðe ſond;

cell.p: wende he ðat non egipcien
ðat hadde it wiſt, ne ſulde a ſen;

row.cell: He thought that none had wist it.

cell.p:
Til after ðiſ on oðer day,
He ſag chiden in ðe wey
two egypcienis, modi & ſtrong,

ðiſ on wulde don ðe toðer wrong;
And moyſes nam ðer-of kep,
And to hemward ſwide[257] he lep,
And vndernam him ðat it agte awold.

row.cell: On the second day he saw two men chiding, and reproved them.

cell.p: And he him anſwerede modi & bold;

row.cell: The wrong-doer thus answered him,

"Meiſter(.) moyſes, quo haueð ðe mad?
ðu art of dede and o word to rad.
"Moses, who made thee master?

cell.p: we witen wel quat iſ bi-tid,

Quuow giſter-dai waſ ſlagen and hid;
ðe bode iſ cumen to pharaun,[258]

row.cell:
[Fol. 53b.]
We know well how yesterday one was slain and hid.
Get ſal ðin pride fallen dun."
Soon shall thy pride fall down."

cell.p: Ðo bi-thowte him moyſes,

And his weige ðeðen ches;
ðurg ðe deſerd a-wei he nam,

row.cell: Then Moses fled

And to burge madian he cam,
And ſette hi[m] ðor vten ðe town,
and came to Midian,

cell.p:
Bi a welle ðo ſprong ðor dun.
Raguel Ietro ðat riche man,
Was wuniende in madian,

row.cell: where dwelt Jethro,

cell.p: He hadde ſeuene dowtreſ bi-geten;
ðor he comen water to feten,

row.cell: who had seven daughters.

And for to wattren here ſep;
(Wimmen ðo nomen of here erf kep,
These maidens took care of cattle.

cell.p: Pride ne cuðe bi ðat dai

Nogt ſo michel ſo it nu mai).
Hirdes wulden ðe maidenes deren,

row.cell: Pride was not so great then as now.

cell.p:
Oc moyſes ðor hem gan weren,
And wattrede here erue euerilc on,
And dede hem tidelike to tune gon;

row.cell: Moses helped the maidens to water the flocks.
And ben ſone hom numen;

And b[i]foren here fader cumen,
And gunen him ðore tellen,
They told their father

cell.p:
Hu a gunge man, at te welle[n],
ðewe and wurſipe hem dede;

row.cell:
[Fol. 54.]
how a young man at the well had protected them.

cell.p:
And ietro geld it him in eſtdede,
Sente after him, freinede hiſ kin,

row.cell: Jethro sent after him and kept him in his house,

cell.p: Gaf him iſ dowter ſephoram;

To wife in lage he hire nam,
And bi-gat two ſunes on hire ðer,
firſt gerlon, ſiðen eliezer.
Egipte king to late waſ dead,
ðe ðe childre ſo drinkelen bead.

row.cell: and gave him his daughter to wife, who bore him two sons.

cell.p: Riche men ðo kepten ſwilc ware.

row.cell: On a time Moses went into the desert with his flocks, for rich men then kept such ware.

ðo ſag moyſes, at munt ſynay,
An ſwiðe ferli ſigt ðor-bi,
fier brennen on ðe grene leaf,
By Mount Sinai he sees a wondrous sight,
a bush burning, and nevertheless green and whole.

cell.p: Vt of ðat buſk, ðe brende and ðheg,
God ſente an ſteuene, brigt and heg;

row.cell: Out of that bush God's voice was heard, clear and high,

"Moyſes, moyſes, do of ðin ſon,
ðu ſtondes ſeli ſtede up-on;
'Moses, Moses, take off thy shoes, for thou standest on holy ground.

cell.p: Hic am god ðe in min geming nam
Iacob, yſaac, and abraham;

row.cell:
[Fol. 54b.]
I am the God of Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.

ic haue min folkes pine ſogen,
ðat he nu longe hauen drogen;
I have seen the affliction of my people,

cell.p: Nu am ic ligt to fren hem ðeðen,
And milche and hunige lond hem queðen;

row.cell: and have come down to deliver them,

div.head: GOD APPEARS TO MOSES AT SINAI.

row.cell:
An .vii. kinge-riches lond
Ic ſal hem bringen al on hond.
and to bring them into the land of seven kingdoms.

cell.p: Cum, ðu ſalt ben min ſondere man,
Ic ſal ðe techen wel to ðan;

row.cell: Come, thou shalt be my messenger,

cell.p: ðat he lete min folc ut-gon;

row.cell: and bid Pharaoh release my people.
If he refuse, I shall work great marvels,

cell.p:
And maken min folc frelike ut-gong;
Ge ſulen cumen wið feteles & ſrud,

row.cell: and cause my people to go out freely.

cell.p:
And reuen egipte ðat iſ nu prud.
Werp nu to token dun ðat wond."

row.cell: As a sign, throw down thy wand." The wand then became an ugly snake.

cell.p: God him bad, bi ðe tail he it nam,
And it a-non a wond it bi-cam,

row.cell: God bade Moses take it by the tail, and anon it became a wand.

And in hiſe boſum he dede his hond,
Quit and al unfer he it fond;

[Fol. 55.]
He put his hand into his bosom and it became leprous.

cell.p: And ſone he dede it eft agen,
Al hol and fer he wiſte it ſen.

row.cell: He put it in again and it became whole and sound.

cell.p:
"If he for ðiſe tokenes two
Ne liſteðe ne troweð to,
Go, get ðe water of de[259] flod
On ðe erðe, and it ſal wurðen blod."

row.cell: "If they believe not these tokens, pour out the water of the flood on the earth, and it shall become blood."

cell.p:
"Louerd, ic am wanmol, vn-reken
Of wurdes, and may ic Iuel ſpeken.
Nu iſ forð gon ðe ðridde dai,
Sende an oðer; bettre he mai."

row.cell: "Lord! I am not eloquent, and cannot speak well," said Moses.

cell.p:
"Quo made domme, and quo ſpecande?
Quo made bisne, and quo lockende?
Quo but ic, ðat haue al wrogt?
Of me ſal fultum ben ðe brogt."

row.cell: Quoth God, "Who made the dumb, the speaking, the blind, and the seeing?"

div.head: MOSES AND AARON ARE SENT TO EGYPT.

row.cell:
"Louerd, ſent him ðat iſ to cumen,
Vgging and dred me haueð[260] numen."

cell.p: "Aaron ðin broðer can wel ſpeken,

ðu ſalt him meten and vnſteken
Him bodeword min, and ic ſal red
Gunc boðen bringen read and ſped."

row.cell: "Aaron, thy brother can speak well, thou shalt meet him, and make known to him my words."

cell.p: Moyſes, frigti, ðo funden gan

row.cell: Moses asks leave of Jethro to visit his brethren.

cell.p: ðog drechede he til god ef[t] bad,

And brogte him bode ðe made him glad,
ðat pharaun, ðe wulde him ſ[l]en,
Waſ dead and hadde iſ werkes len.

row.cell:
[Fol. 55b.]
Moses delayed until God's message again came to him.

cell.p: MOyſes and hiſe wif ſephoram,

And hiſe childre wið him nam;
And ðat on waſ vncircumciſ.

row.cell: Then he departed with his wife and children.

cell.p:
He nam ſo forð, ſoð it is;
An angel, wið an dragen ſwerd,

row.cell: One child was uncircumcised, and the angel in the way sought to slay him.

cell.p: Sephora toc ðiſ gunge knaue,

And dede circumciſe haue,
And gret, and wente frigti a-gen,

row.cell: Zipporah circumcised her son.

cell.p:
And let moyſes forð one ten.
He bar hiſe gerde forð in iſ hond,
And nam a weie[261] bi deſerd lond;

row.cell: Moses pursued his way alone.

cell.p: Moyſes him haueð iſ herte[262] vt-dragen,

row.cell: At Mount Sinai he meets with Aaron.
They come into Egypt.

cell.p: And let hem ſen tockenes fro gode;

row.cell: The people believe them.

div.head: GREATER LABOURS ARE LAID UPON THE ISRAELITES.

row.cell:
He redden ſamen he ſulden gon
wið[263] wiſe men to pharaon.

cell.p: "God," he ſeiden, "of iſrael
ðe bode ſente, and greteð wel,

row.cell: Moses and Aaron come before Pharaoh,

cell.p:
ðat, bi ði leue, hiſe folc vt-fare,
ðre daiges gon and ben ðor gare,
In ðe deſerd an ſtede up-on,

Hiſ leue ſacrifiſe to don."
Quad pharaun, "knowe ic[264] him nogt,
Bi quaſe read haue ge ðiſ ſowt?"

row.cell: and deliver their message.

cell.p: Seide moyſes, "ic am ſonder man,

Egipte folc me knowen can,
for ic am ðat ilc moyſes,

row.cell: Moses says that he is well known to the Egyptians,

cell.p:
ðe egypte folc of ſorge les,
ðan ethiops woren her cumen;

ic warc al ðat ðu was binumen,
And ſwanc and michel ſorwe dreg,

row.cell: having delivered them from the Ethiopians,

cell.p:
Get iſt vnſene hu ic it bi-teg?
Ic haue ben ſiðen at munt ſyna,
Godes bode-wurd bringe ic ðor-fra."

row.cell: and that he brings God's message from Mount Sinai.

cell.p: ðat ðu beſt cumen nu eft agen;

row.cell: Pharaoh chides Moses,

ðiſ folc, ðat ðu wilt me leden fro,
ſal ben luken in more wo."
and declares that the Israelites shall suffer still greater woe.
Ðe king it bad, and [it] wurð don;
[Fol. 56b.]

cell.p:
More ſwinc ðo was hem leid on.
Hem-ſeluen he fetchden ðe chaf
ðe men ðor hem to gode gaf,
And ðog holden ðe tigeles tale,
And elten and eilden,[265] grete & ſmale.

row.cell: More labour is laid upon the Israelites.

cell.p:
Ðo fleg ðiſ folc wið moyſen,
And [he] to god made hiſe bimen.
"Louered, qui waſ ic hider ſent?
ðin folc iſ more in ſorwe went."

row.cell: Moses complains to God.

div.head: MOSES AND AARON PERFORM MIRACLES BEFORE PHARAOH.

row.cell: God renews his promise by his name Adonai,

cell.p: Min milche witter name eley

row.cell: which was unknown to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

cell.p: Moyſes told hem ðiſ tidding;

ðog woren he get in ſtrong murni[n]g.
Siðen ſpac god to moyſen,
and tagte him hu it ſulde ben.

row.cell: Moses told the Hebrews these tidings, and yet were they in great anguish.

cell.p: fowre ſcore ger he waſ hold,
And aaron ðre more told,[266]

row.cell: Moses was now fourscore years old.

Quanne he ðat[267] bodewurd ſpoken,
And deden ðe firme token.

cell.p: AAron ðor warp vt of hiſ hond

Moyſeses migtful wond,
And it wurð bi-foren pharaon

row.cell: Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh.

An Iglic ſnake ſone on-on;
ðe king ſente after wiches kire,
It became an ugly snake.

cell.p:
Wapmen ðe weren in ſowles lire,
ðe ferden al bi fendes red,
fendeſ hem gouen ſinful ſped;
And worpen he ðor wondes dun,

row.cell: The sorcerers, by the devil's help, did the like.

cell.p:
fro euerilc ðor crep a dragun;
Oc moyſes wirm hem alle ſmot,

row.cell: Each of their rods became a dragon.

cell.p:
And here aldre heuedes he of bot;
ðog deden wicheſ ðo men to ſen

row.cell: Moses's serpent bit off their heads.

div.p: At the bottom of this page is the catchword—"Quanne he ðat bodewurd."

div.head: THE WATERS ARE TURNED INTO BLOOD.

cell.p: And pharaon ſtirte up a-non,

And for-bed ðiſ folc to gon.
ÐO ſeide moyſes to araon,
"Quat redeſ tu, broder, ſule wit don?
ðiſ king him his[268] wel wiðer-ward
Agen ðis folc, and herte hard;

row.cell: Pharaoh would not let the Israelites go.

Go we and ſpeken wið hem get,
And fonden wið ðiſ token bet."
Moses and Aaron again came before Pharaoh.

cell.p: And ſo deden [he] ſone a-non,

And comen bi-foren pharaon,
Quad aaron, "nu ſaltu ſen
Quilc godes migtful ſtrengðes ben."

row.cell: [Fol. 57b.]
He ſmot on ðat flod wið ðat wond,
Aaron smote on the flood with his wand;

cell.p: Sone anon blod men al it fond;

row.cell: soon anon it became blood,

And ðe fiſſes, in al ðat blod read,
floten a-buuen and wurðeden dead;
and the fish in it died.

cell.p: In euerilc welle, in euerilc trike,
men funden blod al witterlike,

row.cell: In every well and pool blood was found,

But-if it were in ðe lond gerſen,
ðor-inne woree[269] ðe ebriſſe men.
ðis wreche, in al egypte rigt,
except in Goshen.

cell.p:
Leſtede fulle ſeuene nigt;
ðo waſ ðiſ king ſumdel for-dred,

row.cell: This plague lasted seven nights.

cell.p:
And het hem he ſulden vt ben led;
And moyſes ðiſ pine vn-dede,
And water wurð on blodeſ ſtede.

row.cell: Pharaoh then promised that the Hebrews should depart.

cell.p: Him ðhugte he maden water blod;

row.cell: When the plague was removed he would not release them.

cell.p:
It waſ on fendes wiſe wrogt,
for to bi-tournen[270] ðe kingeſ ðogt.
Moyſes lerede god, ſpac him mide,
Al ðat iſ broðer aaron dede.

row.cell: Mad sorcerers misled the king.

Eft he comen to pharaon,
And he wernede ðiſ folc ut-gon.

div.head: THE PLAGUES OF FROGS AND GNATS.

cell.p: And aaron held up his hond,

row.cell: Aaron held up his hand towards the water, and up came a host of frogs.

cell.p: Summe woren wilde, and ſumme tame,
And ðo hem deden ðe[272] moſte ſame;

row.cell: Some were wild and some tame.

In huſe, in drinc, in metes, in bed,
It cropen and maden hem for-dred;
Some crept into houses, drink, meat, and bed.

cell.p: Summe ſtoruen and gouen ſtinc,
And vn-hileden mete and drinc;

row.cell: Some died and stank.

cell.p:
Polheuedes, and froſkes, & podes ſpile
Bond harde egipte folc [273]in ſile.
ðiſ king bad moyſes and aaron,
ðat he ſulden god bone don;

row.cell: Tadpoles, frogs, and toads afflicted Egypt's folk.

And ſone ſo moyſes bad iſ bede,
ðiſ wirmes ſtoruen in ðe ſtede;
The frogs died,

cell.p: And quane ðe king wurð war ðis dead,

row.cell: but the king forbad the departure of the Hebrews.

cell.p: He ſmot wið ðat gerde on ðe lond,

And gnattes hird ðor ðicke up-wond,
ſmale to ſen, and ſarp on bite,
In al egypte fleg ðiſ ſmite.

row.cell: The third plague of gnats, small to look at, but sharp in biting.

cell.p: And ðo dede men and herf wo,
Anger and tene, ſorge and wo.

row.cell: [Fol. 58b.]

Quoðen ðo wiches clerkes(.) "ðiſ
fortoken godeſ gaſtes is."
The sorcerers said, "This is token of God's ghost,"

cell.p: Her hem wantede migt and ſped,

to ſwilc ðing cuðen he non red;
ðiſ toknes dede aaron.

row.cell: for they lacked might to do this.

cell.p:
God ſente ſiðen hem oðere on,
for euere eld ðiſ king on-on,

row.cell: Pharaoh remained obstinate,

div.head: PLAGUES OF FLIES, BOILS, AND BLAINS,

row.cell: Sei him, if min folc ne mote gon,
and was punished by a plague of flies.

cell.p: And ðuſ[274] it was, and al ðiſ ſor

Sag pharaun, and dredde him ðor.
He gaf hem leue ðo vt to faren
wið-ðanne-ðat he to londe ef[t] charen;
And moyſes bad meðe here on,

row.cell: Then gave he them leave to depart,

cell.p:
And ðiſ fleges fligt vt iſ don;
And pharaon wroð[275] herte on hard,
And vn-dede hem ðat[276] forward.
Moyſes ſpac ſiðen wið gode,

row.cell: and the flight of flies was removed.

cell.p: And he brogte pharaun ðiſ bode;

row.cell: Message comes to Pharaoh of a great plague.

"To-morgen, bute he mugen vt-pharen,
Egyptes erf ſal al for-faren."

cell.p: He wið-held[277] hem and, al-ſo he it b[e]ad,

Al ðe erf of egipt wurð dead;
And get ne migte ðiſ folc vt-gon,
ſwilc har[d]neſſe iſ on pharaon.
After ðiſ time, it ſo bi-cam,
ðat moyſes aſkes up-nam,

row.cell: The murrain among the cattle.
The plague of boils and blains.

cell.p:
ðe wicches hidden hem for-ðan,
Bi-foren pharaun nolden he ben,

row.cell: The sorcerers hid themselves, and would not come before Pharaoh,

cell.p:
So woren he lodelike on to ſen;
At laſt, quan it waſ ouer-gon,

Hadde moyſes ðo leue non.
Siðen ſente ðe louerd gode,

row.cell: so loathsome were they to look upon.

cell.p:
bi moyſes, to ðiſ king bode;
"for-ði lete ic ðe king her ben,

Men ſal, ðurg ðe, min migte ſen,
And knowen ſal ben, ðe to un-frame,
In euerilc lond min migte name.

row.cell: God's message to Pharaoh.

cell.p: ſwilc hail was her or neuere nomen

row.cell: He threatens the king with hail-storm.

cell.p: ðo men, ðe weren in eige and dred,
ben borwen, and erue, ðurg ðiſ red.

row.cell: [Fol. 59b.]

O morgen, al ſwilc time al ſir,
ðhunder, and hail, and leuenes fir,
Cam wel vnghere; al ðat it fond
On the morrow came thunder, hail, and lightning.

cell.p:
ne derede it, coren, ne erf, ne men;
ðo ſeide ðe folc to pharaon,

row.cell: It slew many men, broke down trees, grass, and corn.

cell.p:
"Nu ic wot we haue miſ-don;
Moyſes, do ðiſ weder charen,

And gu ſal [ic] leten ut-faren."
Moyſes gede vt, helde up iſ hond,
And al ðiſ vnweder ðor atwond,

row.cell: The Egyptians beseech Moses to remove this plague.

cell.p: And wurð ðiſ weder ſone al ſtille,
And al after ðe kinges wille.

row.cell: The storm ceased,

ðiſ weder iſ ſofte, And ðiſ king hard,
And brekeð him eft ðat forward.
MOyſes ſiðen, and aaron,
but though the weather was soft, the king's heart was hard.

cell.p: Seiden bi-foren pharaon,

row.cell: Then said Moses,

cell.p: ðat men ſulen longe ðor-after ſpeken."

row.cell: "To-morrow shall the grasshoppers come into the land."

"Goð vt," quað he, "red ic ſal taken,
And gu ſiðen i ſal anſwer maken."

cell.p: Qvað ðiſ folc, "beter iſt laten hem vt-pharen,
Al ſal egipte elles for-faren."

row.cell: The Egyptians advise the king to let the Israelites go.

He calde hem in; quad pharaon,
"Quilc ben ðo ðe ſulen vt-gon?"
Pharaoh is at first inclined to let them go,

cell.p: Quað moyſes, "but alle wapmen,
wið erf, and childre, and wimmen."

row.cell: but would only grant permission to the men.

cell.p: MOyſes held up hiſ hond,

row.cell: Moses held up his hand, and a southern wind uprose,

cell.p: ðiſ wind hem brogte ðe ſkipperes,
He deden on greſ and coren deres.

row.cell: which brought the locusts.

ðat lond was ful, and ðiſ king wo,
He ſente after ðe breðere ðo.
Quad pharaon, "ic haue miſ-numen,
Then was the king full of woe,
and besought Moses to turn from them the evil.

cell.p: And ſo [he] dede, and on wind cam

row.cell:
[Fol. 60b.]
A western wind took away the locusts.

cell.p: Hiſ herte ðo wurð ðwert and hard,

And al he brac hem [ðat] forward.
MOyſes ſiðen held up iſ hond,

row.cell: Pharaoh broke his covenant.

cell.p:
And ðhikke ðherkneſſe cam on ðat lond,
ðat migte non egipcien

Abuten him for mirkneſſe ſen;
Manige ðor ſorge on liue bead,

row.cell: The plague of thick darkness.

And manige weren rewlike dead;
Quor-ſo ðe folc waſ of yſrael,
Many died from fear.

cell.p:
He adden ligt and ſowen wel.
ðo quad pharaon to moyſen,

row.cell: The Israelites had light.
"Led vt al ðat iſ boren of man,
The king tells them to go, and

cell.p: And let her hen boden er[f] & ſep,

ic wile ðor-on[278] nimen kep."
Quad moyſes, "la! god it wot,

row.cell: to leave their flocks and herds behind.

cell.p:
ſal ðe[r]-of bi-leuen non fot,
Al we ſulen iſ wið vs hauen;

'Wold,' quad god, 'wile ðor-of crauen.'"
Quað pharaon to moyſen,

row.cell: Moses will not consent to this arrangement.

cell.p:
"Nu ic rede ðat ge flen;
for ſe ic gu more-ouer nu,
dead ſal be[279] wreken ouer gu."

row.cell: Moses and Aaron are driven out from the presence of Pharaoh.

MOyſes fleg to lond gerſen,
ðor wuneden hiſ kinnes men.

cell.p: Quað god, "get ic ſal pharaon,

row.cell: God tells Moses of his final vengeance upon the Egyptians.

cell.p: Deigen ðor ſal ilc firme bigeten

Of men and erf, non forgeten;
Oc among gu, dredeð gu nogt,
to gu ne ſal non iuel ben ſogt,
Ne ſal ic gu nog[t] loten
Of ðat ic haue gu bi-hoten."

row.cell: Each first-born shall be destroyed.

Siðen quað god to moyſen,
"ðiſ ſal gure firmeſt moneð[280] ben,
ðoo gune men ðe mone ſen
The year shall begin,

cell.p:
In april Reke-fille ben."
ðanne he lereden hem newe wunen;

row.cell: when in April the new moon is seen.

"Euerilc ger, more to munen,
Euerilc huſ-folc ðe mai it ðauen
The institution of the Passover.

cell.p:
So mikil hird ſo it noten mai,
Ben at euen folc ſum to ſamen,

row.cell: A lamb or kid of the first year is to be taken and slain by each household on the fourteenth day of the month,
And ilc folc iſ to fode framen,
and to be roasted whole.
And eten it bred, and non bon breken,
[Fol. 61b.]

cell.p:
And nogt ðor-of vt huſe wreken,
Oc ſod and girt, ſtondende, and ſtaf on hond,

row.cell: None of it is to be taken out of the house.
Ilc man after his owen fond,
It is to be roasted whole,

cell.p: Heued and fet, and in rew mete[n],

leſen fro ðe bones and eten,
Wið[281] wriðel and vn-lif bread;"

row.cell: and eaten with bitter herbs, and unleavened bread.

cell.p:
ðe bi-leuen brennen he bead.
"ðe dure-tren and ðe uuerſlagen,

row.cell: The remainder is to be burnt, and the blood is to be sprinkled upon the door-posts.

cell.p: ON midel ſel, ðat[282] ilc nigt,
So cam wreche on egipte rigt;

row.cell: Vengeance came upon the Egyptians.

cell.p: lich-leſ, ſo manige dead ðor kipte.[283]

row.cell: The first-born of man and beast were slain.

cell.p: And ſwiðe a-weiward hem garen.

row.cell: Pharaoh consented to let Israel go.

cell.p: for here ſwinc-hire he nu hauen;

row.cell: The Egyptians gave the Hebrews whatever they asked.
Gold and ſiluer he hauen vt-brogt,

cell.p:
ðe tabernacle ðor[286]-wið wurð[287] wrogt;
He woren ſexe hundred ðhuſent men,

row.cell: The Israelites numbered 600,000 men.

cell.p: Almost redi waſ here fare,

moyſes bi-ðogt him ful gare
Of ðat ðe iſ kin haueð ſworen,

row.cell: Moses thought of the oath sworn to Joseph.
Ioſepes bones ſulen ben boren;
Joseph's grave could not be found.

cell.p: Oc ðe ail haueð[288] ſo wide ſpiled,
ðat hiſ graue iſ ðor vnder hiled,

row.cell:
On an gold gad ðe name god
Iſ grauen, and leid up-on ðe flod;
A golden rod with the name of God upon it was laid upon the flood.

cell.p: Moyſes it folwede ðider it flet,

And ſtod ðor ðe graue under let;
ðor he doluen, and hauen ſogt,
And funden, and hauen up-brogt
ðe bones ut of ðe erðe wroken,

row.cell: Moses followed its course, and thus discovered the grave.
Some of the bones were whole and some broken.

cell.p: Quane he geden egipte fro,
It wurð erðe-dine, and fellen ðo

row.cell: When Israel left Egypt there was an earthquake.

fele chirches and ideles mide,
Miracle it was ðat god ðor dede.
Many temples fell down.

cell.p: Gon woren .vii. ſcore ger

Siðen[289] ioſep waſ doluen ðer;[290]
And .xxiii. ſcore fro ðan
ðat god it ſpac wið[291] abrahram.

row.cell:
[Fol. 62b.]
Seven score years were gone since Joseph was buried.

cell.p: fro Rameſe to ſokoht ſtede

Non man on hem letting dede,
For ſwinc and murning hem was on,
fro ðe liches in-to ðe erðe don;
And manige of ðo greten forði
ðat he adden ben hard hem bi.

row.cell: The Israelites journey from Rameses to Succoth.

cell.p:
To burg ethan fer fro ſokoth,
And ðeðen he ten to pharaoth;[292]
ðor he ſtunden for to ſen
quilc pharaon wið hem ſal ben.

row.cell: From Succoth they go to Etham, and thence to Pihahiroth.

Pharaon bannede vt hiſ here,
Iſrael he ðhogte to don dere;
Pharaoh called out his army.

cell.p: Sex hundred carte-hird i-wrogt[293]

row.cell: Six hundred chariots he brought out of Egypt, fifty thousand horsemen, and ten score thousand men of foot.

div.head: THE ISRAELITES CROSS THE RED SEA.

cell.p: Alle he ledde hem vt forði
ðat folc ebru to werchen wi.

Ðiſ godes folc waſ under-numen,
Quan he ſegen ðiſ hird al cumen,
Sore he gunen for-dredde ben,
for ne cuðen ne[295] gate flen,

row.cell: When the Israelites saw the Egyptian host they became sore afraid.
And if he ðore ben bi-ſet,

Ille he ſulen ben hunger gret;
He ne mogen figten a-gen,
for they were without weapons.

cell.p:
for [he] wið-vten wopen ben;
ðanne he ðuſ woren alle in dred,
On moyſen he ſetten a gred.
"Beð nu ſtille," quað moyſes,

row.cell: They chided Moses.

cell.p:
"ðor god wile(.) iſ non helpeles;
Ge ſulen ſen ðiſ ilke dai
Quat godes migt for gu mai."
He bad ðiſ folc dregen wið ſkil,
And he bi-ſogte godes wil.

row.cell: Moses promises them God's assistance.

cell.p:
Qvað god, "quor-at calles ðu me?
Hold up ðin gerde to ðe ſe
And del it ſo on ſundri del,
ðat gu ben garknede weigeſ wel."

row.cell: God instructs Moses to stretch out his rod over the sea.
ðo moyſes helde up hiſ hond,
Moses did so.

A wind blew ðe ſe fro ðe ſond;
On twel[fe] doles delt iſt ðe ſe,
A wind blew the sea from the sand,

cell.p:
xii. weiges ðer-in ben faiger and fre,
ðat euerilc kinde of iſrael
Mai ðor hiſ weige finden wel.

row.cell: and twelve thoroughfares were made for the people.

cell.p: ðe water up-ſtod, ðurg godes migt,

row.cell: The water stood up as a wall on both sides.

cell.p: Oc moyſes gede in bi-foren,

row.cell:
[Fol. 63b.]
Moses went first, and then the men of Judah.

div.head: THE EGYPTIAN HOSTS ARE DROWNED.

cell.p: Bi-foren hem fleg an ſkige brigt

ðat nigt hem made ðe weige ligt;
Egiptes folc gunnen ðiſ ſen,

row.cell: A cloud went before them.

cell.p:
And wenden ðat he wode ben.
Ðis bode herde king pharaon

And him ðuhte ſellic ðer-on,
Garkede his hird & after nam,

row.cell: Pharaoh pursued the Israelites,
And to ðe ſe bi nigte he cam;
and to the Red Sea he came.

cell.p: In ferde ðiſ hird after ðiſ king,

row.cell: In went this host after the king.

cell.p: ðo quoðen he, "wende we a-gen,

An[d] iſrael folc lete we ben."
ðor-quiles ben ðo kinges[296] cumen

row.cell: Some were for going back.

cell.p:
Ouer, and hauen ðe londes numen;
Egipcienes woren in twired wen

queðer he ſulden folgen or flen;
And moyſes ſtod up-on ðe ſond,

row.cell: The Israelites reached the land,

cell.p:
God him bad helden up hiſ hond
to-ward ðiſ water, in a morgen quile
ðe ſe luked, ſo god it wile,[297]

row.cell: and God bade Moses stretch his rod over the sea.

And on and on, ſwiðe litel ſtund,
Egypcienes fellen to ðe grund;[298]

[Fol. 64.]
The sea covered the Egyptians,

cell.p: Of hem alle bi-leaf non fot

Vn-drincled in ðat ſalte ſpot.[299]
Ðvs iſ iſrael of hem wreken,
And here welðe iſ to londe weken,
Wepen, and ſrud, ſiluer, and gold;
wel hem mai ben ðe god beð hold!

row.cell: and not one remained undrowned in that salt spot.

Moyſes ðor made a newe ſong,
And tag[t]e it al ðat folc a-mong;
Moses made a new song, and taught it to the people.

cell.p: And ilke dai ðat ſeuen nigt,
Ones he ðor it ſungen rigt;

row.cell: Each day for a week it was sung over.

div.p: At the bottom of this page is the catchword—"And on and on."

div.head: THE SOJOURN AT SHUR, ELIM, AND SIN.

cell.p:
ðor-of in eſterne be we wunen
Seuene ſiðes to funt cumen.
Ðor quiles he weren in ðe deſert,

row.cell: In memory of which are we wont to come seven times to the font at Eastertide.

cell.p: Ðe fifte ſuriuren ðat he deden,
In ðe deſert ſur, on drie ſtede;

row.cell: The fifth sojourn was in the wilderness of Shur;

ðre dages weren he ðider gon,
ðat he ne funden water non;
three days the people were without water.

cell.p: A welle he funde at marath,[301]

ðe water was biter and al wlath;[302]
A funden trew ðor-inne dede

row.cell: At Marah the waters were bitter, but
Moyſes, and it wurð ſwet on ðe ſtede.
a tree rendered them sweet.

cell.p: Ðe ſexte ſuriuren at elim,

xij welle-ſpringes weren on him,
An[d] then[303] and ſexti palme tren
bi ðo welles men migte ſen;
He maden ſiðen, fro elim,

row.cell:
[Fol. 64b.]
The sixth sojourn was at Elim,

cell.p:
Mani ſuriuren in ðe deſert ſin.
Bi-twen elim and ſinay,

row.cell: and from thence to Sin.

cell.p:
bred wantede, hem was wo forði;
ðat was on ðe ðrittiðe[304] dai,

ðat here wei fro egypte lay,
ðor he woren hungur for-dred;

row.cell: Bread fails them.

cell.p:
"Ille," he ſeiden, "haue we ſped,
Bet uſ were in egipte ben,

Bred and fles ðer[305] we muwen ſen."
Moyſes wurð war ðe folc was wroð,
And here gruching ðo god was loð.
"ſtille," quað he, "and on-dreg,
Godeſ fulſum-hed iſ gu ful neg."

row.cell: They murmur against Moses.

cell.p: So fele so he wulden raken;

row.cell: God sends them a flight of fowls,
and on the morrow a dew,

cell.p: It lai ðor, quit als a rim[306] froſt,

row.cell: like rime frost;

He ðe it ſogen,[307] ſeiden, "man hu,"
Manna for-ði men clepeð it nu.
"Man-hu," said they, wherefore they called it Manna.

cell.p: Quad moyſes, "loc! her nu [iſ] bread,

Ille gruching iſ[308] gu for-bead."
A met ðor was, it het Gomor,

Ilc man iſ he bead, and nunmor,
Him gaderen or ðe ſunne-ſine,
Elles he ſulden miſſen hine.

row.cell: Each man gathered an omer of it before the sun shone,

for it malt at ðe ſunne-ſine,
Oc oðer fir for-hadede hine.
for it melted at the sunshine.

cell.p: To duſt he it grunden and maden bread,

row.cell: When ground and made into bread, it tasted like wafers made with honey.

cell.p: Moyſen dede ful ðe gomor,

In a gold pot, for muning ðor.
Held it ſundri in clene ſtede,

row.cell: Moses filled an omer of the manna,

cell.p:
And in ðe tabernacle he it dede.
Wið ðiſ mete weren he fed,

fowerti winter vten leð,[309]
Til he to lond canaan
Comen(.) ðat god hem giuen gan.

row.cell: and placed it in the tabernacle.

cell.p: Forð nam ðiſ folc, ſo god tagte him,
to ðe deſert of rafadim;[310]

row.cell: Forth came this folk, and came to Rephidim,

Tidlike hem waſ ðat water wane,
ðor he grucheden for ðriſt hane;[311]
where they murmured for thirst, and did chide with Moses.

cell.p: Harde he bi-haluen ðer moyſes,

And to god he made is bi-men.
"Louered," quad he, "quat ſal ic don?
He ſulen me werpen ſtones on."

row.cell: [Fol. 65b.]

cell.p: Quað god, "go ðu to erebiſ ſton,
And ſmit wið ðin gerde ðor-on."

row.cell: God sent him for water to a rock in Horeb.
It was a ſtede henden ðor-bi,

cell.p:
On a ſyde of munt ſynay;
And he ſmot wið his wond ðor-on,
And water gan ðor-vten gon;

row.cell: Moses smote the rock,

Anog adden he ðanne drinc,
Redi funden wið litel ſwinc;
and the people had enough to drink without toiling for it.

cell.p: ðat ſtede waſ cald temptatio,
for he ðo god fondeden so.

row.cell: This place was called Temptation.

cell.p:
Amalec, yſmaeles ſune,
Was ðor hende rafadim[312] wune,
He welte ðor ſtone and iaboch,

ðat herdes folc him louerd toch;
Wopened he ben a-gen iſrael.

row.cell: Amalek comes to war against Israel.

cell.p:
Moyſes ear it wiſte wel,
And ſente agen hem king ihesum,

wið folc iſrael wopened ſum;
He let bi-aften ðe[313] more del,

row.cell: Moses sends Joshua with the army to fight with Amalek.

cell.p:
To kepen here ðing al wel.
He, and aaron, and hur ben gon,
Heg up to a dune ſone o-non;

row.cell: Moses, accompanied by Aaron and Hur, goes up to the top of a hill, and prays for the folk of Israel.

cell.p:
Amalechkes folc fledde for agte of dead,
And quane he let[314] iſ hondes niðer,
Amalech folc fagt hard and wiðer;
Quane it wurð war, vr[315] and aaron

He iſ under-leiden wið an ſton,
Til ſunne him ſeilede in ðe weſt;

row.cell: Amalek is overcome by the holding up of Moses' hands.

cell.p:
ðus fagt Moyſes ðor alðer-beſt.
Amalech fleg, and iſrael

Hadde hegere hond, and timede wel.
ðo ſente god to moyſen,
wið ðis timing to muning ben,

row.cell: Thus Moses fought best of all.

cell.p: "Get ſal ðe kinde of amalech
Ben al fled dun in deades wrech."

row.cell: The future destruction of Amalek.

Moyſes made ðor alter on,
"Min bliſ" iſ name ðor-one don.
Moses raises an altar.

cell.p: ÐO cam ietro to moysen,
To ſpeken him and ðo kinnes-men,

row.cell: Jethro visits Moses,
bringing with him Zipporah and her two sons.
Moses relates to him the destruction of Pharaoh.
And at wið moyſen feſtelike,
[Fol. 66b.]

cell.p:
And tagte him ſiðen witterlike
Vnder him helpes oðere don,
ðat folc ſtering to ſtreng[t]hen on.

row.cell: Jethro counsels Moses to appoint rulers of the people,

cell.p: Al bi ðhuſenz ðiſ folc was told,

Ilc ðhuſent adde a meiſter wold;
And vnder ðiſ tgen[317] ſteres ben,

row.cell: rulers of thousands,

Ilc here on hundred to bi-ſen;
Vnder ðis ilc two ſteres wunen,
rulers of hundreds,

cell.p: And vnder hem fif oðere numen;

row.cell: rulers of fifties,

Ilc of ðe .v. ſteres-men
Vnder hem welden in ſtere tgen.[317]
and rulers of tens.

cell.p: If ymong .x. wurð ogt miſ-don,

Here ſtere rigten [ſulde] ðor-on,
And if he ne mai it rigten wel,

row.cell: An appeal to be made from the ruler of ten,

Taunet iſ meiſter euerilc del;
And if he rigten it ne can,
to the ruler of hundreds,
and thence to the superior ruler.

cell.p: If it ne mai or rigted ben,
ſo ſal it cumen to moysen.

row.cell: The final appeal to be made to Moses.

cell.p:
He bad him cheſen ſtereſ-men
Migti, ðe gode-frigti ben,
ðe ſoð-faſtneſſe lef ben,
And ðe niðing [and] giſcing flen.

row.cell: These rulers were to be able men, god-fearing, lovers of truth, and haters of covetousness.

cell.p: Al[ſ] he redde, al-ſo gan it ben.

row.cell:
[Fol. 67.]
Moses accepts the counsel.

cell.p: ðat he nomen fro egipte awei,

row.cell: In the third month of the year Exodus, and in the forty-seventh day after they left Egypt,

cell.p:
Vnder ðiſ munt he funden ſteden,
And here teldes ðor he deden.
On oðer daiges morgen quile,

God tauned[318] moyſi quat he wile.
"Sei ðiſ folc ðat nu ðolen,

row.cell: the people come to the desert of Sinai.

cell.p:
for iſ here ðhogt nogt me for-holen;
'If ye liſten lefful to me,

Ic wile min folc owen be.'"
And moyſes tolde ðiſ iſrael,
And him heten euerilc del,
ðat hem bideð, ſulen he don.
God dede moyſes ðiſ bodeword on,

row.cell: God's message by Moses unto the people out of the mount.

cell.p: If erf or man ðor-one take,

row.cell: The people are to be prepared against the third day.

It dead ðolen, wið ſtones ſlagen,
Or to dead wið goren dragen;
The mountain must not be touched.

cell.p: ðiſ frig[t]ful [folc] ðus a-biden,
Quiles ðiſ daiges for[ð] ben gliden."

row.cell: [Fol. 67b.]

cell.p:
Ðe ðridde daiges morge quile,
ðunder and leuene made ſpile,
On ðiſ munt ſtod, and ſkies caſt,
And dinede an migtful hornes blast;

row.cell: On the third day there were thunders and lightning and a thick cloud upon the mount.

cell.p: ðiſ folc wende hauen for-loren hine;[321]

row.cell: Smoke up reeked and the mount quaked.
Oc he cam faiger and fer him to,

cell.p:
And gan wið hem ſpeken ſo;
"Ilc gure wel in herte mune,
Ne iſt nogt moyſes, amrame ſune,

row.cell: Moses addresses the people.

cell.p:
And let adam fonden ðe tre
ðe noe barg, and abraham

row.cell: He reminds them of their deliverance from the Egyptians,

cell.p:
Ledde vt in-to lond canaan;
Of olde abraham and of ſarra bigeten
Digere[322] or eiðer child or wif.

row.cell: and of God's kindness to their ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac, and Joseph.

Cumeð her forð, and beð alle reken,
And lereð wel quat he ſal ſpeken."

cell.p: He ledde hem to ðe muntes fot,
ðat alle he it herden witterlike.

row.cell: Moses leadeth the people to the foot of the mount.

cell.p: Min wreche iſ hard, min ðole iſ long.

row.cell:
The Ten Commandments.
First Commandment.

cell.p:
Tac ðu nogt in idel min name[n],
Ne ſwer it les to fele in gamen,
Ne let ðu nogt min wurðfulhed
for-faren in ðe fendes red.

row.cell: Third Commandment.

Min hali dai ðu halge wel,
An do ðin dede on oðer ſel.
Fourth Commandment.

cell.p: Wurð ðin fader and moder ſo,
ðat ðu hem drede and helpe do.

row.cell: Fifth Commandment.

cell.p: for truke of ðin helpe an[d] read.

row.cell: Sixth Commandment.

Oc horedom ðat ðu ne do,
Ne wend no lecherie to.
Seventh Commandment.

cell.p: Loke ðe wel ðat ðu ne ſtele,
Ne reflac, ne ðefte, for-hele.[324]

row.cell:
[Fol. 68b.]
Eighth Commandment.

Falſe witneſſe ðat[325] ðu ne bere,
Ne wið ðe leſe non ma[n][326] ne dere.
Ninth Commandment.

cell.p: Ne giſce ðu nog[t] ðin neſtes ðing,

row.cell: Tenth Commandment.

cell.p: Ðiſ for-frigted folc figeren ſtod,

dredful, and bleð, and ſori mod;
Herden ðat dredful beames blaſt,
Sogen ðat figer, dred held hem faſt.
ðo ſeiden he to moyſen,

row.cell: The Israelites at the foot of the mount are in great dread and fear.

cell.p:
"Be ðu nu god and us bi-twen,
Her nu quat god ſal more queðen,
And tellet uſ ſiðen her bi-neðen."
And moyſes ſteg up a-non,

row.cell: They intreat Moses to stand between them and God.

cell.p:
God hem bad bodes manige on
And lages; and hu he ſulen maken
ðe tabernacle, and wor-of taken

row.cell: God gave to Moses many commandments and laws,

cell.p: ðe gold, and ſiluer, and ðe bras,

ðe ſyðen don ðor-on[327] was,
And nemeld it beſeel,

row.cell: instructed him concerning the making of the Tabernacle,

cell.p:
And two oðere to maken it wel;
And gaf to[328] tabeles of ſton,
And .x. bodeword writen ðor-on.

row.cell: and gave him two tables of stone upon which were written the Ten Commandments.

Ðor quiles moyſes was up wið gode,
And liſtenede al ðat leue bode,

cell.p: Swilc wod-hed ðiſ folc[329] cam on,
ðat he ſeiden to aaraon,

row.cell: The people, in the absence of Moses, said unto Aaron,

cell.p:
"Mac vs godes foren us to gon,
of moyſes haue we helpe non."
Aaron and vr ſtoden a-gen,

And boden hem ſwilc ðhowtes leten;
ðat wod folc ðor ur of dage

row.cell: "Make us gods to go before us,"

cell.p:
Brogten, and deden aaron in age;
Here faigere ringes he boden taken,

And don in fier, and geten, and maken
An calf of gold, and [an] alter
Made ðat folc, and lutten it ðer,

row.cell: and compelled him to make a molten calf,

cell.p: And ðat calf ofrendes deden,

And made gret feſt in ðat ſtede[n].
Ðo ſeide god to moyſen,

row.cell: which they worshipped.

cell.p:
"Go ðu nu dun ðin folc to ſen,
He hauen ſineged and miſdon,
Let me taken wreche ðer-on."

row.cell: God is angered thereby.

cell.p:
Egipte folc ſal ðor-of ben fagen,
And ſeyen ðat he ben bi-ſwiken,
In ðe deſert wel liðerlike;[331]

row.cell: Moses intreateth for them.

cell.p: And ðenk, louerd,[330] quat ben bi-foren
Abram, and yſaac, and iacob ſworen."

row.cell: [Fol. 69b.]
God listeneth to Moses, and is appeased.

cell.p:
And Ioſu cam him a-gen,
Alſ he was ilc dai wune to don,
quil moyſes ðat munt was on.
Quat Ioſue to moyſi,
"Ic wene he figten dun her-bi,"

row.cell: Moses came down with the tables,

div.head: THE IDOLATERS ARE SLAIN.

row.cell:
"Nai, for gode," quad moyſes,
"It iſ a ſong wikke and redles."

cell.p: Moyſes cam ner and ſag ðiſ plages,[334]

row.cell: and seeing the idolatry of the people, he brake them in pieces.

cell.p: And dede ðat calf melten in fir,

And ſtired it al to duſt ſir,
And mengde in water and forð it of,
And gaf ðat folc drinken ðat drof.
ðo wiſte he wel quilc hauen it don,

Sene it was here berdes on.
ðo gredde he lude, "goð me to,
Alle ðe god luuen so."

row.cell: The calf he burnt and ground to powder, and mixed it with the water they drank.

cell.p: Frend ne broðer ne ſpared he nogt
On of hem ðat haued ðiſ wunder wrogt;

row.cell: Moses caused the idolaters to be put to death.
Of ðo ðe weren to ðiſ red,

cell.p:
.xxx. hundred to ðe dead
woren ðane don ſone a-non,

row.cell: The number slain were about 3000.

cell.p: Ðo woren on liue ſumdel les.

On oðer dai quad moyſes,
"Michel ſinne haue ðe[335] don,[336]
Ic ſal gon ſeken bote her on."

row.cell: On the morrow, Moses reminded the people of their sin.

cell.p: Eft he ſteg up to munt ſynay,

for to bi-ſeken god merci.
"Louerd," quad he, "ðin meðe iſ god,
Merci get for ðin milde mod![337]
Or ðu ðiſ folc wið milche mod,[338]
Or do min name ut of ðin boc."

row.cell: He returned to Mount Sinai to seek God's mercy.
God promises to send his angel before the people.

div.p: MS. Michel ſinne quað haue ðe don.

cell.p:
Sal ic don ðe bi-foren gon."
Ebrus ſeigen it waſ michael
Engel ðe ſiðen ledde hem wel.
Moyſes faſtede ſiðen to pligt
xl. daiges and xl. nigt;

row.cell:
Oðere tables he brogte eft(.) writen,
And ſunne-bem brigt ſon iſ wliten
Moses received other tables.

cell.p: ðat folc on him ne migte ſen
But a veil wore hem bi-twen.

row.cell: [Fol. 70b.]

cell.p: And oðer metal ſwilc he wolde;

row.cell: The Israelites offer Moses gold and silver for the tabernacle.

cell.p:
He it bi-tagte beſſeleel,
And eliab, he maden wel
ðe tabernacle alſ hem was tagt,
Goten and grauen wið witter dragt;

row.cell: Bezaleel and Aholiab are appointed for the work of the tabernacle.

cell.p: Ne ſwilc ſafte her on werlde brogt;

row.cell: Seven months they were about it.

cell.p:
God it tagte al ear moyſen
Wiſlike hu it wrogt ſulde ben,
Quilc ſrud, quat offrende, quilc[339] lage,
And quat for luue, and quat for age.

row.cell: God taught Moses the fashion of it.

cell.p:
Aaron biſſop, oðere of ðat kin,
Sette he hem for to ſeruen ðor-in.
Bokes he wrot of lore wal,

Hu ðiſ folc hem rigt leden ſal,
Betten miſ-dedes, and clene lif
Leden, wið-uten [h]ate and ſtrif.

row.cell: Aaron and others of his kin were appointed to serve in the tabernacle.

cell.p: Twelf moneð forð ben alle cumen,
Or he fro ſynay ben forð numen;

row.cell: Twelve months passed ere the people departed from Sinai.

[Fol. 71.]
On the twentieth day of the second month (in the second year),

cell.p:
And ðiſ folc ðor after teg.
ðre dages and nigtes faren it gan

row.cell: the Israelites departed from Sinai,

And wið-ſtod in ðe deſerd pharan;
ðiſ folc iſ after ſofte togen,
and came into the wilderness of Paran.
For their complaining,

cell.p: fier iſ on hem bi-ſiden ligt,
fele it brende and made o-frigt,

row.cell: the fire of the Lord consumed them,

cell.p:
Moyſes it bleſſ[ed]e wið his bede,
And brenninge he calde ðat ſtede.
Here hine-folc ðe waſ hem mide,
And ſumme of hem ðor ille dede,

row.cell: but is quenched by the prayers of Moses.

cell.p: And he to god made his bi-men.

row.cell: The people lust for flesh and loathe manna.

cell.p: Ðu ſalt me raðe don[344] ðolen dead."

row.cell: Moses complains of his charge.

Quað god, "ches ðe nu her ſeuenti
Wiſe men to ſtonden ðe bi,
God commands him to choose seventy wise men to help him in the government of the people.

cell.p: And ic ſal hem geuen witter-hed,

And he ðe ſulen don helpe at ned;
And ðin folc ſal to-morgen bi-geten
ynog fles(.) into a moneð[345] for to eten."
Moyſes was bliðe an glad[346] of ðis,

row.cell: [Fol. 71b.]

cell.p:
And ches ðo men [ðe] god made wiſ;
waſ here non of herte dim,
prophetis he weren and holpen him.
Fro lond ortigie cam a wind,

row.cell: The appointment of seventy elders.
Quails are sent in wrath at Kibroth-Hattaavah.
Two daiges hem ben fugeles cumen,
For two days the fowls came.

div.head: MIRIAM IS SMITTEN WITH LEPROSY.

cell.p: ðat gruching hauen he derre bogt,

row.cell: The Lord smote the people with a plague because of their murmuring.
FOrð he nomen to aſſaroth,
The people come to Hazaroth.

cell.p:
ðor wurð maria ſumdel ſoth,[349]
for ſche ðor haueð wið moyſes fliten;

row.cell: Miriam speaks against Moses,

cell.p:
ðor wurð ghe ðanne wið lepre ſmiten,
And vten ſundred .vii. nigt,
In grot and in ſrifte, ſore offrigt;[350]

row.cell: and is smitten with leprosy.

Moyſes bi-ſogte, and ſche wurð fer
And frend, and cam ðat[351] broðer ner.

cell.p: FOrð nam ðiſ folc ſiðen fro ðan

row.cell: The people remove from Hazaroth and come to Paran.

cell.p: Fro ðeðen[352] he ſente forð to ſen,

Quilc ðo riche londes ben,
ðat god hem ſulde bringen in;

row.cell: Men are sent to search the Land of Promise.

cell.p:
On man he ſente of ilc kin.
xii. ſondere men ðor vte faren,
ðiſ hoten lond ðurg-vt he charen,

row.cell: One is sent from each tribe.

cell.p: ðeſ .xii. ðider hem hauen brogt

row.cell: The spies having been away forty days,

cell.p:
Of ðe plenteð ðe god ðor gaf,
An win-grape on an cuuel-ſtaf,
And tolden hem ðe lond iſ god,
ful of erf and of netes brod;

row.cell: return bringing with them of the plenty of the land.

Oc burges ſtronge and folc v[n-]frigt,
ſtalwurði to weren here rigt;
In Hebron they found walled cities, stalworth men, and giants.

div.p: At the bottom of the page is the catchword—"Moyſes bi-ſogte, &."

cell.p: And geteniſſe men ben in ebron,
Quilc men mai get wundren on.

row.cell:
ðiſ folc ðo ſette up grot and gred,
And ſeiden he folwen iuel red;
The Israelites murmur at the news.

cell.p: "Betre iſ vs get we wenden agen

And in egipte ðralles ben,
ðan we wurðen her ſwerdeſ ſlagen,

row.cell: [Fol. 72b.]

cell.p:
And ure kin to ſorge dragen;[353]
An loder-man we wilen us ſen,
And wenden in-to egipte agen;

row.cell: "A captain," said they, "we will make, and return into Egypt."

cell.p:
Ðo quad Ioſue and calef,
"Leateð ben ſwilc wurdes ref,
And doð nogt god almigten wrong,
Iſ milce iſ mikel, iſ ſtrenge iſ ſtrong."

row.cell: Joshua and Caleb endeavour to still them.

ðor ðrette god hem alle to ſlen,
If moyſes ne wore ðor agen;
God threatens them.

cell.p: Oc for iſ benes and for iſ ſake[n],
get he ſal wið hem milche maken,

row.cell: For Moses' sake he spareth them.

cell.p:
or mor ut of egipte told,
ðat hauen ðuſ often fand,
Ne ſulden welden ðat leue land,

row.cell: The murmurers are deprived of entering the land.

cell.p: Wið-vten Ioſue & calef,
Here rigt-wiſed waſ gode lef.

row.cell: Joshua and Caleb are excepted.

Moyſes told hem al ðis anſwere,
And he ben ſmiten in ſorweſ dere;
Much sorrow came upon the people.

cell.p: Get he ſulen .xxx.vii. ger
In ðe deſert ben vten her.

row.cell: Yet thirty-seven years shall they be in the desert.

cell.p:
Agen he maden here dragt,
Al-ſo ðat ſkie haueð[354] tagt.
Oſwas was moyſes eam,[355]
And chore was iſ bernteam;

row.cell:
Ille nið iſ herte wexe on
A-gen moyſen and aaron,
Korah, with two hundred and fifty princes, rebel against Moses.

div.head: THE REBELLION OF KORAH AND ABIRAM.

cell.p: Hem two .ii. hundred men,
And two[356] ðo .xl. and ten;
Meiſtres princes he wolden hem maken,

row.cell: They said they were more worthy to perform the services of the Tabernacle.

On dathan(.) an oðer Abiron.
Moyſes it herde and ſeide a-non,
"To-morwen beð her alle redi,
Dathan and Abiram were joined to Korah.

cell.p:
And ilc gure oðer ſtonde bi;
And ilc gure hiſe reklefat,
And fier ðor-inne and timinge on ðat,
And ðan ſulde we brigte ſen,

Quilc gure ſal god quemest ben."
And ðuſ it waſ on morgen don,

row.cell: Moses' directions to the company of Korah.

cell.p:
Ne wulde he, dathan(.) ne abiron,
For orgel pride forð ðor cumen;

row.cell: Dathan and Abiram would not obey the command of Moses.
Moyſes ðor gret and bad iſ bede,
[Fol. 73b.]

cell.p:
And erðe denede[358] ſone in ðat ſtede,
And opnede vnder [h]ere fet;
Held up neiðer ſton ne gret,
Alle he ſunken ðe erðe wið-in,

Wið wifes, and childre, and hines-kin,
Swilc endeſið vn-bi-wen hauen;

row.cell: The earth swallowed up Korah.

cell.p:
darð[359] noman ſwinken hem to grauen,
ðiſ erðe iſ to-gidere luken,

Als it ne were neuere or to-broken.
FOr chore wel wiſte ðat

row.cell: None had need to toil in burying them.

Gret fier wond vt of is reclefat,
And of iſ fere on and on,
A fire came from God,
and burnt the two hundred and fifty men.

div.head: A PLAGUE SLAYS FOURTEEN THOUSAND PEOPLE.

cell.p: Of ðo Reklefates for wurðing,

Woren mad, and for muning,
Corunes at ðe alter of bras,
ðe at here tabernacle was.

row.cell: Of the censers were made crowns for the altar of brass.

cell.p: For al ðiſ, oðer day ðor waſ neſt,

Agenes moyſes and iſ prest
Gan al ðiſ folc wið wreðe gon,
And wulden hem werpen ſtones on;
To ðe tabernacle he ben flogen,
ðor [h]aueth a ſkie hem wel bi-togen;

row.cell: On the morrow the people murmured against Moses and Aaron, who fled to the Tabernacle.

cell.p:
A fier magti ðat folc feſt on,
And haueð manige ðor for-don.
ðan bad moyſes aaron,

wið hiſe Rekelefat, to ðat fir gon;
And he it dede[360] alſ he him b[e]ad,

row.cell:
[Fol. 74.]
A fire slew many of the people.

cell.p:
Ran and ſtod tuen[361] liues and dead,
And ðiſ fier bleſſede and wið-drog,
It [h]adde or ſlagen manige ynog;

row.cell: Aaron stays the plague.

.xiiii. ðhusent it haueð ſlagen,
And .iiii. ſcore of liue dragen.
Ðog ðiſ folc miðe a ſtund for-dred,
Fourteen thousand and eighty were thus slain.

cell.p:
ðog he ben get in ſunder red,
Get he aglen on here red(.) and wen
ðat it mai loked betre ben;
ðog ðiſe brende ben for-ſaken,
ðog he wenen ðat god ſal taken

row.cell: The Israelites do not recognise Aaron's authority,

cell.p:
Of ðo .xii. tribuz ſumme mo,
To ben ðor he for-hu-gede ðo,
Or ynog raðe of euerilc kin,

He wile ðat ſumme ſerue ðor-in.
"Childre," quat moyſes, "gure ſtrif

row.cell: but think that others are fitted for the service of God.

dereð ðe ſowle and greueð ðe lif;
Do we uſ alle in godes red,
Moses addresses the people,
and directs each prince of the tribes to take a rod, and to write every man his name upon it.

cell.p: And on [ilc] wond writen ſal ben

row.cell: [Fol. 74b.]

cell.p: ðuſ it was don, and on a wond

Wið-uten[362] ðo wrot he wið hond
ðe twelfte names of ðat kin;

row.cell: The rods were written upon,

cell.p:
ðe tabernacle he dedis in,
And ðor he iſ haued god bi-tagt,
And let iſ ben ðor al ðat nagt.

row.cell: and laid before the Lord in the Tabernacle.

cell.p: Alſ ſwilc alſ he iſ dede ðor-in;

row.cell: On the morrow the rods were examined,

cell.p:
Oc on, ðe was of aaron,
(Writen was name leui ðor-on),
It was grene and leaued bi-cumen,

And nutes amigdeles ðor-onne numen;
ðo wiſten he ðat[363] aaron

row.cell: and Aaron's rod, of the house of Levi, had budded, blossomed, and brought forth almonds,

cell.p:
Was hem biſſop ðurg god don;
To ſen gode witneſſe ðor-on,

ðat wond was in ðat arche don.
[I]N ðe deſert he wuneden ðor

row.cell: so it was seen that God had appointed Aaron as bishop.

cell.p:
.xxx.vii. winter and mor;
Longe abuten munt ſeyr,
folgede hem ðat ſkie ſcir,

row.cell: Thirty-seven years and more the people abode in the desert,

[Fol. 75.]
wandering about from place to place,

cell.p:
Alle he[364] olde deden ðor fin.
And at ðe laſte ne-ðe-les,
Eft he come ſone to cades,

row.cell: and all the old ones died.

cell.p: ðor was moyſes ſiſter dead;

row.cell: At Kadesh Miriam died,

div.head: THE DEATH OF AARON AT HOR.

cell.p: Hire lich iſ biried in munt ſin,

Hire ſowle iſ reſted ſtede wið-in.
It bi-tidde after hire dead

row.cell: and her body was buried in Mount Zin.

cell.p:
ðat ðis folc ſorge in ðriſte abead.
And ðer roſ wreððe and ſtrif a-non
Agen moyſen and aaron;

row.cell: The people murmur for water.

cell.p:
God [bad] ſemelen folc and gon,
And foren hem ſmiten on ðe ſton
And ſeide, ut of ðe ſmiten ſton

row.cell: Moses is commanded to gather the people before the rock at Meribah.
Moses smote the rock twice, and the water flowed forth,

cell.p: ðo flew ðor[365] water michil and ſtrong,
Al folc and erue a-nog a-mong.

row.cell:
[Fol. 75b.]
and the folk and cattle had enough.
The people are denied a passage through Edom.

cell.p: Til ðat[366] he comen to munt hor;
Aaron ðo wente of liwe ðor,

row.cell: They come to Mount Hor,

Eleazar, iſ ſune, him neſt
Was mad biſſop and meiſter preſt.
where Aaron dies.

cell.p: xxx. daiges ðat folc in wep

row.cell: Thirty days the folk mourned for him.

cell.p: vii. ſcore ger and .iii. told,

ðor he lið doluen on ðat wold.
Forð ðeðen he comen to ſalmona,

row.cell: The age of Aaron.
for-weried grucheden he ðoa,
The people murmur,
ðor-fore hem cam wrim-kin among,

cell.p:
ðat hem wel bitterlike ſtong;
Non oðer red ðor don ne waſ,

row.cell: and are plagued with serpents.

cell.p:
Moyſes ðor made a wirme of bras,
And henget hege up-on a ſaft,
ðurg godes bode and godes craf[t];

row.cell: They, repenting, are healed by a serpent of brass,

Quat ſtungen man so ſag ðor-on,
ðat werk him ſone al was vn-don;

cell.p: Digere it was al ðat berem-tem,[367]

row.cell: which long afterwards was worshipped in Jerusalem.

cell.p: Frigti nam forð ðis folc and bleð,

row.cell: The people come to Zered.

cell.p: King ouer(.) amor(.) reos(.) ſeon,

row.cell: Sihon, king of the Amorites, comes out against Israel and is overcome.

cell.p:
Oc he ſlugen king of baſaan.
To lond moab drugen he ſo,
ðor nu iſ a burg, ierico.
Balaac king was for-dred for-ðan,

And ſente in to lond madian,
To hiſe frend ðe ben him neſt;

row.cell: The king of Bashan is slain.

cell.p:
And ſente after balaam ðe preſt,
Wið riche men an[d] giftes oc,

for to ſtillen hiſe [vn-]eðe mod,
And bad him cumen for to don

row.cell: Balak sends after Balaam,
fol[c] of yſrael hiſ curſing on.
to curse the folk of Israel.
Balaam wið-[h]eld him ðor ðat nagt
[Fol. 76b.]

cell.p:
To witen quat him ſal wurðen tagt;
Al waſ iſ fultum and hiſ ſped

row.cell: The failure of the first message.

div.head: BALAAM SETS OUT TO CURSE ISRAEL.

cell.p:
Bi-luken ille, in fendes red.
On nigt him cam ſonde fro gode,
Agen ðiſ kinges[369] red for-bode,

And ðat he ne curſe non del
ðiſ folc ðat god bliſcede wel.
O morgen ſeide he, "fare ic nogt,
for bode iſ me fro gode brogt."

row.cell: God forbids Balaam to curse the Israelites.

cell.p:
Balaac ſente richere an[d] mo
Medes, and oðer men to ðo.
"Sondes, ſondes," quað balaam,
Or he ðeſe oðere medes nam,

row.cell: Balak's second message to the prophet.

cell.p:
"Ðog balaac king me goue hold,
Hiſ huſ ful of ſiluer and of gold,
Ne mai ic wenden her bi-neðen;"

Godes wurd iſ cumen alſ it iſ queðen;[370]
Oc or or ge wenden agen,
ðiſ nigt ic ſal fonden and ſen."
Quat tiding so it cam on ðe nigt,
On morgen, at ðe daiges ligt,

row.cell: Balaam's answer to the messengers.

cell.p: Wicke giſcing it haueð[371] al wrogt.

row.cell: He consents to go with the princes of Moab,
ðuſ rideð forð ðiſ man for-loren,
being influenced by covetousness.

cell.p:
An angel drog an ſwerd him bi-foren,
ðiſ aſſe wurð ſo ſore of-dred,

Vt of ðe weige it haueð him led.
Sellic ðogte balaam for-ði,
And bet and wente it to ðe ſti
Bi-twen two walles of ſton;

row.cell:
[Fol. 77.]
An angel meets him in the way. The ass is frightened,

cell.p:
Eft ſtod ðiſ angel him a-gon,[372]
ðiſ aſſe iſ eft of weige ſtired,[373]
So ðat balames fot iſ hird;[374]

row.cell: and turns aside to the wall,

cell.p: And he wurð ðo for anger wroð,
And ðiſ prikeð and negt ſloð;

row.cell: so that Balaam's foot is crushed.

forð and narwere ðiſ aſſe him bar,
And ðe ðridde ſiðe wurð ðe angel war.
ðo ne migte ðes aſſe flen,
The angel went further, and stood in a narrow place,

cell.p:
Ne he ne durſte forðere ten,
Oc fel ðor dun(.) ðan ðis was don,

row.cell: and the ass fell down under Balaam,

Balaam it ſpureð and ſmit ðor-on;
And god vndede ðiſ aſſes muð,
who smote her with his staff.

cell.p:
So ſoð it iſ(.) ſo it is ſelcuð.
Quuað ðiſ aſſe ðus wið vn-miðe,
"Qui betes ðu me ðis ðridde ſiðe?"
Quað balaam, "for ðu tregeſt me;
Had ic an ſwerd, ic ſluge ðe."

row.cell: God opened the mouth of the ass, and she spoke to her master.

So was ðis were to wunder brogt,
ðhog ðe aſſe ſpac, frigtede he nogt;
Nevertheless this infatuated man was not frightened.
ðe let god[375] him ðat angel ſen,
[Fol. 77b.]

cell.p:
wið ðe ſwerd dragen him agen.
Quað ðe angel, "ðin weige iſ me loð,

row.cell: The angel tells Balaam,

cell.p:
ðor-fore am ic wið ðe ðuſ loð;[376]
If ðin aſſe ne were wið-dragen,
Her ſuldes ðu nu wurðen ſlagen."

row.cell: that but for the ass he would have slain him.

Quað balaam, "quane ic haue miſ-faren,
If ðu wilt, ic agen ſal charen."
The prophet offers to return.

cell.p: "far forð," quað ðe angel, "oc loc ðe wel,
for-bi min red, quað ðu non del."

row.cell: He is cautioned by the angel.

cell.p:
And balaam ſeide him to wiſ,
"Sal ic non wurd[377] mugen forð-don,
Vten ðat god me leið on."

row.cell: Balak entertains Balaam.

cell.p: Balaac him leddede[378] heg on an hil,

And .vii. alteres wrogte in his wil,
On ilc alter fier alðerneðer,

row.cell: Balak causes seven altars to be built.

cell.p:
And ðor-on an calf and a weðer,
And he bad balaac ſtonden ðor-bi,
And gede on-rum qui[379] bute for-ði,

row.cell: On each altar was offered a bullock and a wether.

fro abuuen cam to him bi-neðen,
Word in herte ðat[380] he ſal queðen;

cell.p: Quan he cam to balaac a-gen,
Swilc wurdes he let vt-ten.

row.cell: God's word comes to Balaam,
"Hu mai ic ðat folc curſen on,

cell.p:
ðor louerd haueð[381] bliſcing don?
ðiſ folk ſal waxen wel and ðen,

And ouer al oðer migtful ben,
Hiſ lif beð bliðe, hiſ ending ſal,
ðe timeð al-ſo ðiſ timen ſal."

row.cell: and he blesses Israel.

cell.p: Balaac miſliked al ðiſ queðe,[382]

And ledde hem ðeðen on oðer ſtede,
To munt faga, for to ſen wel
Of folc iſrael ðe oðer del.

row.cell: Balak is greatly displeased.

cell.p: He wente on oðer ſtund or ſtede,

Betre timing ðor-fore he it dede,
And wende wenden godes ðogt,
Oc al he ſwinked him for nogt.

row.cell: He brings the prophet to another place.

cell.p: Hef[t] haueð he mad her .vii. alter,

And on ilc brend eft twin der.
Gede eft balaam up on-rum,
ðo ſeide ðuſ quanne hem cam dun,

row.cell: Again seven altars were raised, and offerings made.

cell.p: "ðis folc, ſprungen of iſrael,

Iſ vnder god timed wel;
Al-ſo leun iſ migtful der,

row.cell: The parable of Balaam.

cell.p:
So ſal ðiſ folc ben migtful her;
ðiſ leun ſal oðer folc freten,
Lond canaan al preige bi-geten."

row.cell: Israel is compared to a lion.

Ille liked ðanne balaac
Euerilc word ðe preſt balaam ſpac.
Balak was ill pleased with the priest's words.

cell.p: Get he ledde him to munt fegor,

And efte he ſacrede deres mor;
ðor[383] ſpac balaam mikel mor
Of ðiſ folckes migt, or he dede or.
"folc ebru," quað he, "ðat ic ſe,

row.cell:
[Fol. 78b.]
Balak brings Balaam to Mount Peor.

cell.p: Bliſced ſal ben ðe bliſcede ðe;

row.cell: Again he blesses the Israelites,

And quuo-ſo wile curſing maken,
Ille curſing ſal him taken;

cell.p: Of ðe ſal riſen ſterre brigt,

And a wond ðe ſal ſmiten rigt
Moab kinges, and under-don
Al ſedes-kin ðiſ werld up-on."

row.cell: and prophesies their future happiness and greatness.

cell.p: Manie tiding quad balaam ðor,

ðe made balakes herte ſor;
Oc ðan balaam wente a-gen,

row.cell: Such tidings made Balak's heart sore.

cell.p:
Tagte he balaam quat migte ben
ðiſ folc to dere, and gaf him red
ðat brogt iſrael iwel ſped.

row.cell: Balaam teaches Balak how to injure the Israelites,

cell.p:
"ðe ginge wimmen of ðin lond,
faiger on ſigte an[d] ſofte on hond,
And brigte on hewe, on ſpeche glad,

Wið ðgere[384] ſal ic ſondes ſad,
ðe ðu ten vt gen ðiſ men,

row.cell: by sending out young women fair of face and soft of speech,

cell.p:
ðe cunen[385] brewen herte-bren,
wið win, and wlite, & bodi, & dwale,
Luue[li]ke and wið ſpeche ſmale,

row.cell: who should "brew heart-burning and love,"

cell.p: And hem fro godes luue led,

row.cell:
[Fol. 79.]
and so turn the people from God.

cell.p:
And fonde to wenden ðuſ here ðhogt,
for wi ne wopen ne helpeð[386] nogt."
forð-nam balaam, ðat ille qu[e]ad
ðe gaf ðiſ read of ſoules dead.

row.cell: For war nor weapon had no power to harm them.
ðuſ it was don, and bi ðat ſel
This counsel was followed,

cell.p:
In ſichin ſingede iſrael,
And for luue of ðiſ hore-plage

Manie for-leten godes lage,
And wrogten ðor ſwilc ſoules for

row.cell: and thus it fell that Israel sinned in Shittim,

cell.p:
ðat he ðor lutten belphegor.
Ðo ſeide god to moyſen,
"ðe me[i]ſtres of ðiſe hore-men,

row.cell: and worshipped Baal-peor.

cell.p: ðise oðer[387] folc ſal meðe ſen."

row.cell: God commands the chief men to be hanged.

Godes wreche ðor haueð of-ſlagen
xx.iii. ðuſent of dagen.[388]
Twenty-three thousand were slain.

cell.p: finees waſ a ſeli man,

row.cell: Phinehas kills Zimri and Cozbi

cell.p: ðurg and ðurg boðen he ſtong

wið hiſe giſarme ſarp & long.
God moysen nemnen bead

row.cell:
[Fol. 79b.]
with his long and sharp pike.

cell.p:
Hiſ folc ðe was firmeſt fro dead,
Or .xx. winter or more hold,
ðe in egypte or ne weren told;

row.cell: God commands Moses to take the sum of the people above twenty.

cell.p: Was non of hem told in tale or,

row.cell: It was found to be 601,720.

cell.p:
ðo moyſes tolde hem and aaron,
ðan [h]e gunnen fro egipte gon.
Vten ioſue and caleph,

Alle elles he driuen in deades weph;
Alle ðiſe wapmen ðor[389] god let liwen,
ðe lond hoten ſal hem ben giuen.
God moyſes clepede and quad to him,

row.cell: Of those who were numbered at Sinai, all died except Joshua and Caleb.

cell.p:
"ſtig hege up to munt Abarim,
And ic ſal don ðe ðeðen[390] ſen
ðe lond ðe ſal ðiſ folc[e]s ben;
ðer ðu ſalt ben of werlde numen.

In to ðat lond ſalt ðu nogt cumen."
"Louerd, merci!" quad moyſes,

row.cell: Moses being told of his death,

cell.p:
"Let ðu ðin folc nogt helpe-les,
And good let oc ðu hem bi-ſe,
Alſwilc alſ hem bi-hu[f]lik bee."

row.cell: intreats God not to let the people be "helpless."

cell.p:
ðat al ðin folc wurð war,
And ðine hondes ley him on,
Sey him on ðin ſtede to gon."
Alſ it is boden, alſo he dede,
Ioſue wurð ſet on hiſe ſtede.

row.cell:
[Fol. 80.]
Joshua is appointed to succeed him.

cell.p:
Ðo moyſes was on abarim,
ðat lond hoten god tawned him.
ðor quiles him leſten liue dages,
Hiſ he tagte leue lages,

row.cell: When Moses was on Abarim, God showed him the promised land.

cell.p:
And writen hem, haueð[391] iſ hem bitagt,
Bute-if he iſ loken hem beð agt,[392]
Erðe and heuene he wittneſſe tooc,
And wrot an canticle on ðat booc,

row.cell: Moses' song, setting forth God's vengeance

ðat ðreated ðo men bitter-like
ðe god ne ſeruen luue-like.
ðo .xii. twelue kinderedes, on and on,
upon those who would not serve Him truly.

cell.p:
He gaf bliſcing bi-leue gon;
At munt nemboc on ðat knol faſga,
Wane he was ſtigen ðeðen ðoa,
Sag ðe lond of promiſſion,
ðurg god[393] him was ſiðen ðat on.

row.cell: The blessings of the twelve tribes.

ðer he ſtarf inne. ðe moab lond,
His bodi was biried wið angeles hond,
Moses dies in Moab, and is buried by angels' hands.

cell.p: ðer non man ſiðen it ne fond,

In to lef reſte hiſ ſowle wond.
Ebrius ſeigen, ðuſ waſ bi-tid,

row.cell:
[Fol. 80b.]
No man ever found his body.

ðat moyſes waſ hem ðuſ hid,
for, migten he finden ðe ſtede,
It was thus hid,

cell.p:
Quor engel-wird hiſ liche dede,
fele ſulden him leuen on,
And leten god; ðat were miſ-don.

row.cell: that the people might not afterwards worship it.

div.head: MAY GOD SHIELD US FROM HELL'S NIGHT!

cell.p: Ydolatrie, ðat waſ hem lef,
ofte vt-wrogte hem ſorges dref.

row.cell:
MOyſes iſ faren, on elde told
fulle ſex ſcore winter old;
Although Moses was 120 years old,

cell.p: And ðog him leſtede hiſe ſigte brigt,

And euerilc toð bi tale rigt.
.xxx. daiges wep iſrael
for hiſ dead(.) and bi-ment it wel.

row.cell: yet his eyesight remained bright, and every tooth was "by tale right."

cell.p: Swilc prophete in folc of iſrael

row.cell: Such a prophet in Israel rose none.

cell.p: Bi-ſeke we nu godes migt,
ðat he make ure ſowles brigt,

row.cell: Beseech we now God's might,

cell.p: ðurg quat we ben to liue numen,

row.cell: that he shield us from Hell's night,

[Fol. 81.]
and bring us all into bliss. Amen!

div.head: NOTES.

p.hi: Man og to luuen ðat rimes ren,
ðe Wisseð wel ðe logede men.

div.p: og, another form of agh, = ow = ought. ren = run = rune, song, story.

logede = lay. It is not necessarily unlearned, ignorant, etc., for O.E. writers frequently use the term in contradistinction to clergy. See Ayenbite, p. 197. "Vor all manere of volk studieþ in avarice, and (both) great and smale, kinges, prelates, clerkes, an lewede and religious."—(Ayenbite, p. 34.)
That was born in Ingeland."—(Met. Hom. p. 4.)
3 loken, to take care of oneself, to direct one's course of life, keep from sin. See Ayenbite of Inwyt, pp. 1, 197, 199, 201.
"Ac alneway hit is nyed to leawede men
that hi ham loki vram þise zenne (avarice)."—Ayenbite, p. 31.
10 ðund is evidently an error for gund = yond, yonder, over. Cp. gu for ðu, ll. 365, 366.
"& þeond þat lond he heom to-draf (B. & ouer al þat lond he drof heom)."—(Laȝ. i. 68.)
12 earuermor = eauermor = evermore. 14 soðe-sagen = soðe-sage = sooth-saw = sooth-saying, true saying.

p.hi: Cristene men ogen ben so fagen,
so fueles arn quan he it sen dagen.

div.p: Christian men ought to be as fain (glad)
As fowls (birds) are when they see it dawn.
17 telled = telleð = telleth. 20 devil-dwale = devil-deceiver, devil-heretic = arch-deceiver, arch-heretic. See l. 67. Cf. maȝȝstredwale = master heretic = arch-heretic, in the following passage:—

lg.l: Þat we nu mælenn ummbe
Wass maȝȝstredwale, an defless þeww,
Þat Arrius was nemmnedd."
Of all this loathsome learned folk
That we now talk about
Was an arch-heretic, a devil's serf
That Arius was named.

div.p: til god srid him in manliched,
till god shrouded (clothed) himself in manhood.
24 bote and red, salvation and counsel. 25 And unspered al ðe fendes sped = undid all the fiend's successful work (luck). 26 halp = Old and Middle Eng. holp = helped, assisted.
P. 2. l. 27 Biddi, an error for bidde?

l.hi: Queðer so hic rede or singe!

lg.l: Give Thou me a propitious opportunity
To show (declare) this world's beginning,
Thee, Lord God, for honour,
Whether-so-ever I read or sing!
thaunen = taunen, show, exhibit.
"Ful wel he [Crist] taunede his luue to man,
Wan he ðurg holi spel him wan."

div.p: The word is very uncommon in O.E. writers. Cp. O.Du. tônen, to show. See ll. 1022, 2034. wurðinge = for worship, honour. wurðinge is a noun, not a participle or gerund. See l. 133. 38 Ear ðanne = ere that.

p.hi: ðo bad god wurðen stund and stede,

div.p: When God bad exist time and space.
43 ðrosing seems to be an error for ðrosim or ðrosem = fog, mist, chaos. Cf. waspene in l. 1440, p. 41, where the correct form is wasteme. aðrusemen, to suffocate, occurs in Ancren Riwle, p. 40.

45 ðu wislike mune = do thou wisely bear in mind. 47 hin = hine = him. 48 or, another form of ar, = ere, before. 49-56 The meaning of these lines may be expressed as follows:—"And of them two [God the Father and God the Son] that dearly love, who wield all here and above, proceeds that holy love, that wise will [the Holy Ghost], that wieldeth all things with right and skill [reason]. Might bad with word light exist; also that might [the Holy Ghost] wieldeth holy consolation, for there are three persons and one counsel, one might, and one godhead." 54 Hali froure = holy comfort, an allusion to the office of Holy Ghost as the comforter.
"Hire uoster moder wes an þe frourede hire."

= Her foster mother was one who comforted her.—(St. Marherete, p. 8.) 58 o sunde[r] sad = on sunder shad, i. e. a-sunder shed = divided apart, separated. It still exists in water-shed, Ger. wasser-scheide. Cf. l. 116. See Hampole's Pricke of Conscience, p. 271, l. 32. Cp. "the schedynge of tonges." (Trevisa's Translation of Higden's Polychron., p. 251.) "The longages & tonges were ischad & to-schift."—Ib. p. 251.
P. 3. l. 63 ðis walkenes turn = this welkin's course. See l. 79. 64 quuad = biquuad = bequeathed, ordained. See l. 117.

p.hi: And euerilc wunder, and euerilc wo.

div.p: And every evil and every woe.
Wunder = misfortune, evil. S.Saxon wundre, mischief, hurt.
"hare lust leadeð ham to wurchen to wundre."
= their lust leadeth them to work to mischief.—(St. Marh. p. 14.)
(See Sir Gawaine and the Green Knyght. Ed. Morris, l. 16.)

71-72 Our ancestors had some strange chronological theories. In the Cursor Mundi we read that Adam was made at undern-tide, at mid-day Eve was drawn from his side, and at noon they both ate the apple, and were thus only three tides in bliss.[396]
ðis ik (ilk?) wort in ebrisse wen.
This same word is in Hebrew opinion (tradition). The true form is wene, "a wene" = in supposition. See Laȝ. l. 18752; Orm. l. 4326; Owl and Nightingale, l. 237.

77 a-gon = agen = again. 78 a-gon = gone. It is our word ago.
